role.sales.export.specialist.title: Export Sales Specialist
role.sales.export.manager.title: Export Sales Manager
scene.buyer_audit_notice.l1: The buyer just sent an audit notice. They will inspect the plant in about a month.
scene.buyer_audit_notice.l2: Our batch records have gaps. Someone has to reconcile them before the audit.
scene.buyer_audit_notice.c1: Volunteer to rebuild the records from the source documents, honestly.
scene.buyer_audit_notice.c1.ok: It takes six long hours, but the records hold together and QC notices.
scene.buyer_audit_notice.c1.fail: You find more gaps than expected and lose the evening to them.
scene.buyer_audit_notice.c2: Say nothing and hope the auditors do not look closely.
scene.buyer_audit_notice.c2.only: The meeting moves on. The gaps are still there.
scene.audit_day.l1: The auditors are on the floor. Keep your answers short and accurate.
offer.pad_forecast.why: Everyone rounds the forecast up a little. Numbers are just a story we tell the board.
scene.sales.shipment_pull_in.l1: The buyer on PO 4471 wants the shipment ten days earlier. They have a promotion locked in.
scene.sales.shipment_pull_in.l2: Line 3 is already full. Ten days means overtime and skipping the final packing check.
scene.sales.shipment_pull_in.c1: Commit to the buyer and push production to make it.
scene.sales.shipment_pull_in.c1.ok: Production squeezes the order in. The buyer is happy and your boss notices.
scene.sales.shipment_pull_in.c1.fail: Line 3 breaks down on Thursday. The shipment leaves late and the buyer complains to your boss.
scene.sales.shipment_pull_in.c2: Explain the real lead time and offer a split shipment.
scene.sales.shipment_pull_in.c2.ok: The buyer accepts half now and half on the original date. Production is relieved.
scene.sales.shipment_pull_in.c2.fail: The buyer is unhappy and copies your boss on the reply. You will have to explain yourself.
scene.sales.shipment_pull_in.c3: Tell the buyer yes and sort it out later.
scene.sales.shipment_pull_in.c3.ok: The buyer is thrilled. You have bought yourself a week, and a problem.
scene.sales.shipment_pull_in.c3.fail: The buyer checks with the factory directly and finds out. Your credibility takes a hit.
scene.sales.rfq_discount.l1: Your new buyer's RFQ arrived with a note: they expect six percent off, or they go to another factory.
scene.sales.rfq_discount.l2: Your approval limit is three percent. Anything above needs the manager's signature.
scene.sales.rfq_discount.c1: Offer three percent and trade it for a larger volume commitment.
scene.sales.rfq_discount.c1.ok: The buyer takes three percent with a volume commitment. A clean deal within your limit.
scene.sales.rfq_discount.c1.fail: The buyer walks away for now. The quote goes cold.
scene.sales.rfq_discount.c2: Ask your manager to approve the discount, with the numbers ready.
scene.sales.rfq_discount.c2.ok: Your manager approves four and a half percent after reviewing the margin. The deal closes properly.
scene.sales.rfq_discount.c2.fail: Your manager asks why you did not hold the line, and the discount is refused.
scene.sales.rfq_discount.c3: Promise six percent now and get the approval afterwards.
scene.sales.rfq_discount.c3.ok: The buyer signs at once. Now you need the approval signed without anyone looking closely.
scene.sales.rfq_discount.c3.fail: Finance spots a discount above your limit on the order. Your manager wants a word.
scene.sales.forecast_meeting.l1: Quarter-end forecast. Head office wants a number that looks strong.
scene.sales.forecast_meeting.l2: Round the pipeline up a little. Everyone does. It gets adjusted next cycle anyway.
scene.sales.forecast_meeting.c1: Give the forecast as you honestly see it, with the assumptions written down.
scene.sales.forecast_meeting.c1.ok: Your boss grumbles but accepts. The assumptions are on record if anyone asks.
scene.sales.forecast_meeting.c1.fail: Your boss is openly annoyed and mentions your KPI review.
scene.sales.forecast_meeting.c2.ok: The number goes up, and so does your boss's mood. A bonus of three million dong lands with the month's pay.
scene.sales.forecast_meeting.c3: Ask for a day to check the pipeline properly.
scene.sales.forecast_meeting.c3.ok: You get the day. The revised number is lower than hoped but defensible.
scene.sales.forecast_meeting.c3.fail: Your boss says there is no time, and puts a number in for you.
scene.sales.payment_overdue.l1: Invoice 2208 for your German buyer is 45 days overdue. It hurts our DSO, and Finance wants you to chase it today.
scene.sales.payment_overdue.l2: Accounts payable says the next payment run is in three weeks. Send us a statement first.
scene.sales.payment_overdue.c1: Send a clear statement and call their AP manager directly.
scene.sales.payment_overdue.c1.ok: The AP manager moves the invoice into the next run. Finance notices you closed it.
scene.sales.payment_overdue.c1.fail: The call goes to voicemail twice. The invoice stays open and Finance asks again.
scene.sales.payment_overdue.c2: Offer a two percent early-payment discount to get the cash this week.
scene.sales.payment_overdue.c2.ok: The buyer pays within days. The discount comes out of your margin, and Finance is pleased.
scene.sales.payment_overdue.c2.fail: The buyer takes the discount but pays late anyway. You lost margin for nothing.
scene.sales.payment_overdue.c3: Tell production to hold the buyer's next order until they pay.
scene.sales.payment_overdue.c3.ok: The buyer suddenly finds the money. The relationship is strained, though.
scene.sales.payment_overdue.c3.fail: The buyer escalates to your boss, who did not know about the hold.
scene.sales.sample_request.l1: A promising prospect in Poland wants free samples of the new ceramic pan, and they want them this week.
scene.sales.sample_request.l2: The sample budget is spent for the month. The reserve stock is for buyer claims only.
scene.sales.sample_request.c1: Follow the procedure: request budget approval and ship in two weeks.
scene.sales.sample_request.c1.ok: The prospect accepts the delay and appreciates the professionalism.
scene.sales.sample_request.c1.fail: The prospect goes cold while waiting. A competitor sends samples first.
scene.sales.sample_request.c2: Take samples from the claims reserve and sort out the paperwork later.
scene.sales.sample_request.c2.ok: The samples ship today. QC has not noticed yet.
scene.sales.sample_request.c2.fail: QC counts the reserve and finds the gap. They want to know who signed it out.
scene.sales.sample_request.c3: Pay the courier yourself and send your own display samples.
scene.sales.sample_request.c3.ok: The prospect gets a pair of samples in three days. It costs you a little, and nobody has to bend a rule.
scene.sales.quality_complaint.l1: Your buyer reports the non-stick coating peeling on about three percent of last month's lot, and asks for a credit note.
scene.sales.quality_complaint.l2: Our inspection passed that lot. Three percent is inside the agreed tolerance.
scene.sales.quality_complaint.c1: Open a formal complaint and ask QC to test retained samples with the buyer.
scene.sales.quality_complaint.c1.ok: The tests confirm a batch problem on one line. The buyer sees you dealing with it honestly, and QC fixes the process.
scene.sales.quality_complaint.c1.fail: The retained samples are inconclusive. It takes weeks, and the buyer is impatient.
scene.sales.quality_complaint.c2: Agree a three percent credit note on your own to close it fast.
scene.sales.quality_complaint.c2.ok: The buyer accepts and the complaint closes. The credit note is above your approval limit, though.
scene.sales.quality_complaint.c2.fail: Finance spots a credit note above your limit and asks who approved it.
scene.sales.quality_complaint.c3: Reply that the damage must have happened in shipping.
scene.sales.quality_complaint.c3.ok: The buyer backs off for now. The forwarder's insurer starts asking questions instead.
scene.sales.quality_complaint.c3.fail: The buyer sends photos taken at unloading. The coating is clearly the problem, and you look evasive.
scene.sales.tet_rush.l1: The plant closes for Tet in two weeks. Every buyer wants their order out before the shutdown.
scene.sales.tet_rush.l2: Three of your orders are still unfinished. Which ones ship first is your call.
scene.sales.tet_rush.c1: Rank the orders by contract penalty and ship the most exposed ones first.
scene.sales.tet_rush.c1.ok: You avoid the two penalties that mattered. The third buyer grumbles but accepts a January date.
scene.sales.tet_rush.c1.fail: A penalty clause you overlooked is triggered. It is small, but your boss remembers.
scene.sales.tet_rush.c2: Ask for weekend shifts so all three ship before Tet.
scene.sales.tet_rush.c2.ok: The weekend shifts work. Production is tired and lets you know it.
scene.sales.tet_rush.c2.fail: A machine fails on the second weekend. Two orders ship, and one misses the vessel.
scene.sales.tet_rush.c3: Promise all three buyers a date before the break and work it out afterwards.
scene.sales.tet_rush.c3.ok: Everyone is happy today, and you have a very tense last week of the year.
scene.sales.tet_rush.c3.fail: Only two orders make it. The third buyer heard your promise and remembers.
scene.sales.buyer_gift.l1: Between us, a smaller order split across two invoices keeps my approvals simple. There would be a coordination fee for you.
scene.sales.buyer_gift.l2: Five million dong. Nothing on paper, nobody harmed. Everyone in this business does it.
scene.sales.buyer_gift.c1: Decline politely and note the conversation in your own records.
scene.sales.buyer_gift.c1.ok: The buyer shrugs and moves on, slightly cooler. Your notes are there if anyone ever asks.
scene.sales.buyer_gift.c1.fail: The buyer takes it badly and stops sharing forecasts with you for a while.
scene.sales.buyer_gift.c2: Accept the fee and split the order.
scene.sales.buyer_gift.c2.ok: The money arrives in cash. The split orders go through without a problem.
scene.sales.buyer_gift.c2.fail: Finance notices two invoices for one shipment. Questions start immediately.
scene.sales.buyer_gift.c3: Tell your boss and the compliance officer about the offer.
scene.sales.buyer_gift.c3.ok: Your boss thanks you. The buyer's purchasing rep is moved to another account, and the relationship resets.
scene.sales.buyer_gift.c3.fail: Your boss shrugs it off as ordinary business and asks you not to make waves.
scene.sales.backdate_invoice.l1: We are two hundred thousand dollars short of the quarter target. The last shipment leaves on the first, but I need it booked before quarter-end.
scene.sales.backdate_invoice.l2: Date the documents the thirtieth. It is only a few days. Nobody checks.
scene.sales.competitor_quote.l1: A factory in Indonesia quoted us eight percent below you on the same pan. Can you match it?
scene.sales.competitor_quote.l2: Our margin cannot take eight percent. Find a way to keep the account.
scene.sales.competitor_quote.c1: Hold the price and sell on lead time, quality and after-sales service.
scene.sales.competitor_quote.c1.ok: The buyer stays, with a smaller order. Quality wins more than price this time.
scene.sales.competitor_quote.c1.fail: The buyer splits the order with the competitor. You keep half the volume.
scene.sales.competitor_quote.c2: Match the price and ask your manager to sign off on the margin.
scene.sales.competitor_quote.c2.ok: Your manager approves a partial match. You keep the account at a thinner margin.
scene.sales.competitor_quote.c2.fail: Your manager refuses and asks why you offered it before asking.
scene.sales.competitor_quote.c3: Promise a special coating spec at the same price, and let production figure it out.
scene.sales.competitor_quote.c3.ok: The buyer is delighted. Production is not.
scene.sales.competitor_quote.c3.fail: Production says the spec is not possible at that cost. You have to walk it back.
scene.sales.overtime_request.l1: I am out sick tomorrow and the customer service line is unmanned. Could you cover my calls? Just the urgent ones.
scene.sales.overtime_request.l2: I know it is not your job.
scene.sales.overtime_request.c1: Say yes and cover the urgent calls.
scene.sales.overtime_request.c1.ok: You get through the day tired. The customer service team will remember it, and so will your inbox.
scene.sales.overtime_request.c2: Decline politely and suggest who else might cover.
scene.sales.overtime_request.c2.ok: They find someone else. Nothing changes, and nothing is lost.
scene.sales.overtime_request.c2.fail: Nobody covers, and a buyer waits a day for an answer.
scene.sales.overtime_request.c3: Ask your boss to arrange cover, so you do not have to.
scene.sales.overtime_request.c3.ok: Your boss assigns someone. You look organized, and the colleague looks a little embarrassed.
scene.sales.overtime_request.c3.fail: Your boss asks why you are sending him problems instead of solving them.
scene.sales.customs_docs.l1: The vessel cuts off tomorrow at noon. The certificate of origin lists the wrong factory address.
scene.sales.customs_docs.l2: If the port checks, the container can be held for weeks. Tell me what you want to do.
scene.sales.customs_docs.c1: Stop the booking and get the certificate reissued properly.
scene.sales.customs_docs.c1.ok: The chamber reissues it in time for the next vessel. A week late, and clean.
scene.sales.customs_docs.c1.fail: Reissuing takes ten days. The buyer is angry about the delay.
scene.sales.customs_docs.c2: Ship on time and correct the certificate afterwards.
scene.sales.customs_docs.c2.ok: Nobody checks. The shipment arrives on time, with a certificate you know is wrong.
scene.sales.customs_docs.c2.fail: The importing port flags the mismatch. The container is held and a fine follows.
scene.sales.customs_docs.c3: Ask the forwarder to arrange a corrected certificate for a small fee.
scene.sales.customs_docs.c3.ok: A corrected certificate appears by morning. You do not ask how.
scene.sales.customs_docs.c3.fail: The corrected certificate turns out to be a poor forgery. Customs notices.
scene.sales.kpi_review.l1: Monthly review. You are at seventy percent of quota, and the quarter is half gone.
scene.sales.kpi_review.l2: What is your plan to close the gap?
scene.sales.kpi_review.c1: Show your pipeline with realistic close dates and name the risks.
scene.sales.kpi_review.c1.ok: Your boss respects the honesty and helps you remove two blockers.
scene.sales.kpi_review.c1.fail: The pipeline looks thin. Your boss is polite, but the pressure is clear.
scene.sales.kpi_review.c2: Promise to catch up and chase every possible order, even the low-margin ones.
scene.sales.kpi_review.c2.ok: You land two extra orders. The volume helps the quota, though the margin hurts.
scene.sales.kpi_review.c2.fail: The chase costs you a month and produces little.
scene.sales.kpi_review.c3: Point out that production delays cost you sales.
scene.sales.kpi_review.c3.ok: Your boss agrees some of it was not your fault, and takes it upstairs.
scene.sales.kpi_review.c3.fail: Production hears about it before the day is over. Nobody feels supported.
scene.sales.fx_price.l1: The dong fell against the dollar this quarter, and our steel costs are in dollars. Your fixed-price contracts just lost margin.
scene.sales.fx_price.l2: Tell me how you want to deal with it.
scene.sales.fx_price.c1: Renegotiate with a currency clause at the next renewal.
scene.sales.fx_price.c1.ok: The buyer accepts a clause for new orders. Finance is relieved.
scene.sales.fx_price.c1.fail: The buyer refuses to touch the contract. You are exposed for the rest of the year.
scene.sales.fx_price.c2: Absorb the loss and keep the buyers calm.
scene.sales.fx_price.c2.ok: Nobody outside the company notices. Your margin report does.
scene.sales.fx_price.c3: Ask production to switch to a cheaper coating supplier without telling the buyer.
scene.sales.fx_price.c3.ok: Costs drop and the buyer notices nothing, yet.
scene.sales.fx_price.c3.fail: The buyer's lab finds the coating change in the next batch test.
scene.sales.new_hire_mentor.l1: Boss asked me to shadow you this week. I have no idea how quoting works here. Could you show me?
scene.sales.new_hire_mentor.l2: I will try not to slow you down.
scene.sales.new_hire_mentor.c1: Set aside proper time and walk them through a real quote.
scene.sales.new_hire_mentor.c1.ok: They learn fast, and your boss hears good things.
scene.sales.new_hire_mentor.c1.fail: They make a mistake on a live quote, and you spend the evening fixing it.
scene.sales.new_hire_mentor.c2: Show them the shortcuts, including the ones that bend the rules.
scene.sales.new_hire_mentor.c2.ok: They are delighted. Corners are now being cut in two heads instead of one.
scene.sales.new_hire_mentor.c2.fail: The shortcuts show up in their first quote, and your name is on the training.
scene.sales.new_hire_mentor.c3: Say you are too busy and point them to the manual.
scene.sales.new_hire_mentor.c3.ok: They find their own way, slowly. Nobody blames you.
scene.sales.trade_fair.l1: There is a housewares fair in Frankfurt in a few weeks. The budget covers one person, and I am open to a case for it.
scene.sales.trade_fair.l2: Convince me it is worth the money.
scene.sales.trade_fair.c1: Prepare a short case with the accounts you could meet and the revenue at stake.
scene.sales.trade_fair.c1.ok: Your boss approves the trip. Three meetings are already booked.
scene.sales.trade_fair.c1.fail: The numbers look optimistic to your boss, and the trip goes to a colleague.
scene.sales.trade_fair.c2: Argue that the buyers expect to see you there.
scene.sales.trade_fair.c2.ok: It sounds reasonable enough. Your boss approves half the budget.
scene.sales.trade_fair.c2.fail: Your boss says every salesperson says that.
scene.sales.trade_fair.c3: Skip it and keep your desk work moving.
scene.sales.trade_fair.c3.ok: The fair goes ahead without you. Your pipeline gets your full attention.
offer.buyer_kickback.why: Everyone in purchasing does it, and nobody is harmed.

scene.sales.finance_inquiry.l1: A number in your file does not match the paperwork. Finance would like a word.
scene.sales.finance_inquiry.l2: Walk me through it. I would rather hear it from you than find it myself.
scene.sales.finance_inquiry.c1: Own up and offer to correct the paperwork.
scene.sales.finance_inquiry.c1.ok: Finance appreciates it. There is a mark on your file, but a small one.
scene.sales.finance_inquiry.c1.fail: Finance accepts the correction but writes it up anyway.
scene.sales.finance_inquiry.c2: Explain it away as a timing difference.
scene.sales.finance_inquiry.c2.ok: Finance accepts it, for now. You would rather not be asked twice.
scene.sales.finance_inquiry.c2.fail: The dates do not support your explanation. Finance notes that too.
scene.sales.finance_inquiry.c3: Say your boss asked you to do it.
scene.sales.finance_inquiry.c3.ok: Finance turns to your boss with new questions. Your boss will hear about this.
scene.sales.finance_inquiry.c3.fail: Your boss denies it, in front of Finance. You are on your own now.
scene.sales.buyer_confronts.l1: I have been hearing things from your factory floor. I would like a straight answer from you.
scene.sales.buyer_confronts.l2: Trust is most of what I buy from you. Do not waste it.
scene.sales.buyer_confronts.c1: Tell them what happened, and what you will do about it.
scene.sales.buyer_confronts.c1.ok: The buyer is not pleased, but respects that you said it to their face.
scene.sales.buyer_confronts.c1.fail: The buyer appreciates the honesty and still trims next quarter's order.
scene.sales.buyer_confronts.c2: Deny it and change the subject.
scene.sales.buyer_confronts.c2.ok: The buyer lets it go, for now.
scene.sales.buyer_confronts.c2.fail: The buyer already has the photos. The conversation ends coldly.
scene.sales.buyer_confronts.c3: Offer a discount on the next order to smooth it over.
scene.sales.buyer_confronts.c3.ok: The buyer takes the discount and lets the matter rest. It costs margin.
scene.sales.buyer_confronts.c3.fail: The buyer takes the discount and still remembers.
scene.sales.compliance_interview.l1: We received a report about a payment connected to your accounts. This is a routine conversation.
scene.sales.compliance_interview.l2: Please tell us in your own words what happened.
scene.sales.compliance_interview.c1.ok: It is a hard afternoon. The company treats it as a serious mistake rather than a firing offence.
scene.sales.compliance_interview.c1.fail: The company follows its policy to the letter. You keep your job, on a written warning.
scene.sales.compliance_interview.c2.ok: Without evidence, they close the file. It stays open in your head.
scene.sales.compliance_interview.c2.fail: They have the invoices and the messages. Lying to them is the worse offence.
scene.sales.compliance_interview.c3: Ask for time, and for someone to be with you.
scene.sales.compliance_interview.c3.ok: They agree to a second meeting. You spend the week thinking.
scene.sales.compliance_interview.c3.fail: The delay reads as guilt. The second meeting is colder than the first.
term.po.def: A buyer's formal, written order: what, how many, at what price, and by when. Once accepted it is a binding commitment.
term.rfq.def: A buyer asks several suppliers to quote a price for specific goods, usually to compare them.
term.dso.def: The average number of days it takes to collect payment after a sale. Lower is better for cash.
term.early_payment_discount.def: A small price cut offered if the buyer pays sooner than the due date, trading margin for cash.
term.credit_note.def: A document that reduces what a buyer owes, for example after a quality complaint. It is money you give back.
term.lead_time.def: How long it takes from accepting an order to delivering it, including production and shipping.
term.split_shipment.def: Sending one order in two or more deliveries, for example half now and half later.
term.approval_limit.def: The most a person may agree to alone, such as a discount percentage. Above it, someone more senior must sign.
term.margin.def: What is left of the price after costs, as a share of the price. Discounts come straight out of it.
term.forecast.def: An estimate of future sales. Production, purchasing and finance plan real spending around it.
term.pipeline.def: The list of deals in progress and how likely each is to close.
term.kpi.def: A number used to judge performance, such as quota reached or first-pass yield. People tend to do what the KPI rewards, which is not always what the company needs.
term.claim.def: A buyer's formal complaint about goods, often asking for a credit, a replacement or a refund.
term.tolerance.def: The defect rate or variation a contract accepts as normal. Inside it, goods pass even if not perfect.
term.penalty_clause.def: A contract term that charges the supplier money for late delivery or other breaches.
term.kickback.def: A private payment to someone for steering business to you, or splitting it in a way that helps them. It is bribery, even if everyone does it.
term.conflict_of_interest.def: When a personal gain could influence a work decision. Most companies require you to declare it.
term.revenue_recognition.def: The accounting rule for when a sale counts as income: usually when risk and control pass to the buyer, not when you wish.
term.internal_audit.def: A team inside the company that checks records and controls, independent of the people whose work it checks.
term.supplier_audit.def: A buyer's inspection of a factory's records, process and conditions before or while it keeps ordering.
term.certificate_of_origin.def: A document stating where goods were made, used by customs to apply duties and trade agreements.
term.forwarder.def: A company that arranges shipping, paperwork and customs for exporters.
term.vessel_cutoff.def: The last moment a container can be delivered to the port to make a given ship. Miss it and you wait for the next one.
term.fx_risk.def: The danger that a currency move changes your real price or cost after you have agreed a price.
lesson.promised_unrealistic_date: A promise you cannot keep is a debt: buyers plan around dates, and trust is what you sell.
lesson.discount_above_limit: Approval limits exist so one person cannot commit the company alone. Breaking them moves risk onto others without their knowing.
lesson.forecast_honest: An honest forecast is unpopular today and useful tomorrow: other teams spend real money on it.
lesson.forecast_padded: Padding a forecast borrows credibility. Production and finance act on it, and the gap shows up later as someone else's problem.
lesson.records_prepared_honestly: Clean records are boring, and that is the point: they let anyone audit you calmly.
lesson.reserve_stock_taken: Taking stock off the books without paperwork turns a small favour into a control failure.
lesson.credit_above_limit: A credit note is real money. Above your limit, someone else has to own that decision.
lesson.blamed_forwarder: Blaming someone else for a defect works until the evidence arrives; then it costs you the trust you were protecting.
lesson.declined_kickback: Declining and writing it down protects you: if it comes out later, your record shows which side you were on.
lesson.accepted_kickback: A coordination fee is a bribe by another name. It gives the giver a hold over you, and it is the kind of thing that turns an error into a criminal case.
lesson.reported_kickback: Reporting an offer early feels costly and is cheap: it ends the pressure and puts the risk on the people who should carry it.
lesson.refused_backdating: Dates on documents are facts. Refusing to change them is uncomfortable once and keeps you safe for years.
lesson.backdated_documents: Backdating ties revenue to a date that did not happen. Auditors compare shipping, invoice and bank dates, and the mismatch is hard to explain.
lesson.shipped_wrong_certificate: A wrong certificate can hold a container for weeks, and the buyer pays for your shortcut in delay and fines.
lesson.paid_for_document: Paying someone to arrange a document is buying a forgery risk. The fee is small and the consequences are not.
lesson.silent_spec_change: Changing a specification without telling the buyer breaks the contract and their trust together, and their lab will find it.
lesson.taught_shortcuts: What you teach a newcomer becomes the habit of the team, including the parts you would not defend.
lesson.came_clean: Owning up early turns a finding into a fix. Finance and buyers forgive errors faster than cover-ups.
lesson.lied_to_finance: Lying to Finance turns a correctable error into a question of character.
lesson.lied_to_compliance: Lying to compliance is often a worse offence than the original act, because it is a decision you make with full information.
lesson.confessed: A full statement rarely saves a career, but it usually keeps it from ending in a worse way.
scene.qc.batch_fail.l1: Lot 2291, twelve thousand pans, failed the coating adhesion test at 4.2 percent against a limit of 3. The vessel cut-off is Friday.
scene.qc.batch_fail.l2: Production needs this on the boat. Tell me what you can sign.
scene.qc.batch_fail.c1: Hold the lot, write the non-conformance and propose a rework plan.
scene.qc.batch_fail.c1.ok: The lot is held and reworked. Production is furious, and your manager backs the record.
scene.qc.batch_fail.c1.fail: The rework takes longer than promised and the vessel sails without it. Nobody thanks you, but nobody can fault the record.
scene.qc.batch_fail.c2: Ask your manager for a deviation waiver with conditions, and tell the buyer.
scene.qc.batch_fail.c2.ok: The waiver is signed with extra checks, and the buyer agrees to accept the lot at a reduced price.
scene.qc.batch_fail.c2.fail: The buyer refuses the lot. You have spent a week of goodwill for nothing.
scene.qc.batch_fail.c3: Retest from a fresh sample until the number comes back under the limit.
scene.qc.batch_fail.c3.ok: The fourth sample passes. The lot ships on time, and nobody asks how many samples it took.
scene.qc.batch_fail.c3.fail: A colleague sees the retest log. Four tests on one lot, with the last one passing, is hard to explain.
scene.qc.borderline_result.l1: The seal test reads 3.04 on a limit of 3.00. The buyer signs off on anything at 3.00 or under. The shipment is waiting.
scene.qc.borderline_result.l2: Between us, nobody would ever see the third decimal if we wrote 3.0.
scene.qc.supplier_no_coa.l1: The new coating lot arrived without its certificate of analysis. The supplier says it is the same formula as last time and the paperwork will follow.
scene.qc.supplier_no_coa.l2: We are out of coating on line 2 by Thursday. Sign it in and we keep running.
scene.qc.calibration_overdue.l1: The balance in the lab went two weeks past its calibration date. Every weight since then is technically unverified.
scene.qc.calibration_overdue.l2: The buyer audit is in three weeks. Do not let this become a finding.
scene.qc.audit_prep_records.l1: The buyer audit is on Monday. The incoming-inspection log has gaps on three days, and the auditors read logs line by line.
scene.qc.audit_prep_records.l2: Can you tidy those up before they arrive?
scene.qc.complaint_trace.l1: Two of our stores report pans with a peeling coating, all from the same lot code. What is your explanation?
scene.qc.complaint_trace.l2: Traceability says it was line 3, Tuesday night, the shift with the new operator. Can we call it an isolated case?
scene.qc.inspector_shortcut.l1: I checked twenty pieces on the last lot instead of eighty. The line was waiting and nothing looked wrong.
scene.qc.inspector_shortcut.l2: Please do not make it a thing. I have done it before and it was always fine.
scene.qc.supplier_gift.l1: A small gift for the lab team, from our family to yours. By the way, our next delivery is a little late, and a light incoming check would help us both.
scene.qc.supplier_gift.l2: It is a very good hamper. Nobody needs to know.
scene.qc.oven_drift.l1: The curing oven on line 3 drifts up by eight degrees after midnight. It has done it for a month. Stopping to fix it costs a full shift.
scene.qc.oven_drift.l2: I can change the controller setpoints to compensate. It takes me two minutes, and nobody would notice.
scene.qc.oven_drift.c1: Write up the drift with the data and ask your manager to stop the line for repair.
scene.qc.oven_drift.c1.ok: The repair is approved for the weekend. Production is unhappy, but the data makes the decision easy.
scene.qc.oven_drift.c1.fail: Your manager postpones the repair for a month. You have a record that you raised it.
scene.qc.oven_drift.c2: Log it as an observation and move on.
scene.qc.oven_drift.c2.ok: It goes into the log. The drift continues.
scene.qc.oven_drift.c2.fail: A batch from the drifting hours fails adhesion. The log shows you knew for a month.
scene.qc.oven_drift.c3: Let the technician change the setpoints to compensate.
scene.qc.oven_drift.c3.ok: The drift is masked. The oven now runs on settings nobody approved.
scene.qc.oven_drift.c3.fail: The compensation fails in winter and a lot is overcured. The changed setpoints are found.
scene.qc.recall_decision.l1: A customer cut a finger on the rim of one of your pans. We have two more reports. Are the rims inspected?
scene.qc.recall_decision.l2: It could be one bad pallet. I would rather not alarm anyone before we know. Let us monitor for a few weeks.
scene.qc.audit_findings.l1: We compared your records with the instruments and the shipping documents. Some entries do not line up. We would like to hear it from you first.
scene.qc.audit_findings.l2: Tell us how these entries came to be.
scene.qc.audit_findings.c1: Explain exactly what happened and offer to correct the records and open a corrective action.
scene.qc.audit_findings.c1.ok: The auditors log it as a serious deviation with a corrective action. You keep your role, with a record that shows you owned it.
scene.qc.audit_findings.c1.fail: The auditors escalate it to the quality director despite the honesty. There will be consequences.
scene.qc.audit_findings.c2: Say it was a clerical slip and promise it will not happen again.
scene.qc.audit_findings.c2.ok: The auditors accept it, for now. They will look harder next time.
scene.qc.audit_findings.c2.fail: The documents show it was deliberate. The auditors now have two problems: the records and what you told them.
scene.qc.audit_findings.c3: Say the procedures were unclear and blame the instructions you were given.
scene.qc.audit_findings.c3.ok: The auditors ask your manager about the instructions. Your manager will remember this.
scene.qc.audit_findings.c3.fail: Your manager shows the written procedure. It was clear, and you are now on record saying otherwise.
scene.qc.compliance_interview.l1: We received a report about a gift from a supplier and about how a safety concern was handled. This is a routine conversation.
scene.qc.compliance_interview.l2: Please tell us in your own words what happened.
scene.qc.compliance_interview.c1.ok: It is a hard afternoon. The company treats it as a serious mistake rather than a firing offence.
scene.qc.compliance_interview.c1.fail: The company follows its policy to the letter. You keep your job, on a written warning.
scene.qc.compliance_interview.c2.ok: Without evidence, they close the file. It stays open in your head.
scene.qc.compliance_interview.c2.fail: They have the messages and the delivery records. Lying to them is the worse offence.
scene.qc.compliance_interview.c3: Ask for time, and for someone to be with you.
scene.qc.compliance_interview.c3.ok: They agree to a second meeting. You spend the week thinking.
scene.qc.compliance_interview.c3.fail: The delay reads as guilt. The second meeting is colder than the first.
lesson.qc_held_batch: Holding a failing batch costs goodwill today and protects the buyer, the brand and you.
fact.retested_until_pass: testing the batch again until it passed
lesson.retested_until_pass: Retesting until a number passes is not testing: it hides a real problem behind a lucky sample.
fact.released_with_waiver: the batch released with a waiver
lesson.released_with_waiver: A waiver is legitimate when the right person signs with conditions and the buyer is told. Silence is what turns it into a problem.
lesson.rounded_result: A limit is a line, not a suggestion: rounding a borderline result to pass turns measurement into opinion.
lesson.flagged_borderline: Flagging a borderline result lets others decide with the facts. It is the job, even when it is inconvenient.
fact.accepted_on_supplier_word: the lot you accepted without a certificate
lesson.accepted_on_supplier_word: Supplier paperwork is part of the product: a lot without proof of what it is carries an unknown risk you are signing for.
lesson.quarantined_lot: Quarantine is cheap insurance: it stops a doubt from becoming a defect in a customer's kitchen.
lesson.backdated_calibration: An out-of-date instrument makes every reading doubtful. Backdating the sticker turns an overdue task into a falsified record.
fact.stopped_use_uncalibrated: the scale you took out of use
lesson.stopped_use_uncalibrated: Taking an uncalibrated instrument out of use is slow and visible, and it is exactly what a calibration system is for.
fact.filled_records: the log entries filled in from memory
lesson.filled_records: A record must be made when the work is done. Filling gaps later, however well meant, is fabrication.
fact.told_the_gap: the gaps you showed the auditors
lesson.told_the_gap: Showing a gap together with a corrective plan is what auditors expect. Hiding it is what they punish.
fact.downplayed_defect: the defect you called an isolated incident
lesson.downplayed_defect: Calling a pattern an isolated incident protects today's mood and puts the buyer, and later you, at risk.
lesson.ignored_shortcut: A process is only as strong as what you tolerate. Looking away is approving.
lesson.reported_shortcut: Reporting a colleague's shortcut is uncomfortable, and usually best done first to them, then up if nothing changes.
lesson.accepted_supplier_gift: A gift from someone whose product you inspect is a conflict of interest, however small. Declare it or decline it.
lesson.declined_supplier_gift: Declining and recording a gift costs a little awkwardness and keeps your signature worth something.
fact.unauthorized_adjustment: the oven setpoints you changed yourself
lesson.unauthorized_adjustment: Changing a process outside your authority, even to fix something real, removes the approval that protects you when it goes wrong.
lesson.escalated_drift: Escalating with data turns a hunch into a decision that someone with authority must own.
fact.delayed_recall_notice: the delay in telling the buyer about the sharp-edge defect
lesson.delayed_recall_notice: When a defect can hurt someone, the clock starts when you know. Every day you wait makes you responsible for what happens.
lesson.flagged_safety_risk: Raising a safety risk early is the job. It costs money and goodwill now, and it saves people later.
fact.lied_to_auditor: what you told the quality auditor
lesson.lied_to_auditor: Lying to an auditor turns a correctable quality gap into an integrity case.
term.coa.def: A document from a supplier showing the tested properties of a specific lot of material.
term.non_conformance.def: A product, process or record that does not meet its specification or procedure. It is logged, investigated and closed, not ignored.
term.deviation_waiver.def: Written permission, from someone with authority, to release product that misses a specification, usually with conditions and notice to the buyer.
term.sampling_plan.def: A rule for how many pieces to inspect from a lot and how many defects are acceptable, so a small sample can stand for the whole lot.
term.specification_limit.def: The value a measurement must not cross for the product to pass. A result on the wrong side fails, however close.
term.calibration.def: Checking and adjusting an instrument against a known reference so its readings can be trusted. It has a due date.
term.traceability.def: Being able to follow a product back to its batch, line, shift and materials, so a problem can be contained.
term.capa.def: A recorded plan to fix the cause of a problem and stop it coming back, with an owner and a date.
term.recall.def: Pulling products back from the market because they may be unsafe or defective, usually with notice to buyers and authorities.
term.quarantine.def: Physically and on paper separating material or product that may be bad, so nobody uses or ships it until it is cleared.
term.lot.def: A quantity made together under the same conditions and identified by one number: the unit that is inspected, released or recalled.
role.sales.export.specialist.blurb: You sell a cookware factory's products to overseas buyers. Your pressures: deadlines, discounts, forecasts, and what you are willing to promise.
role.qc.specialist.title: Quality Control Specialist
role.qc.manager.title: QC Manager
role.qc.specialist.blurb: You are the quality gate of a cookware factory. Your pressures: release dates, borderline results, supplier favours, and what you are willing to sign.
offer.release_out_of_spec.why: It is only a few tenths over, the buyer will never notice, and the boat will not wait.
scene.qc.borderline_result.c1: Record 3.04, flag it as borderline and ask for a second measurement.
scene.qc.borderline_result.c1.ok: The second analyst reads 2.98. You record both, and the lot passes on the record.
scene.qc.borderline_result.c1.fail: The second reading is 3.05. The lot fails, and production is unhappy, but the record is clean.
scene.qc.borderline_result.c3.ok: The lot ships. The raw sheet says 3.04 and your report says 3.0.
scene.qc.borderline_result.c3.fail: The buyer's lab measures 3.04 on the same lot and asks why your report says 3.0.
scene.qc.borderline_result.c2: Check what the buyer contract says about measurement uncertainty before deciding.
scene.qc.borderline_result.c2.ok: The contract allows for measurement uncertainty of 0.05, so 3.04 passes, and you record why.
scene.qc.borderline_result.c2.fail: The contract has no such clause. Your manager asks why you did not check before asking.
scene.qc.supplier_no_coa.c1: Quarantine the lot until the certificate arrives.
scene.qc.supplier_no_coa.c1.ok: The certificate arrives Wednesday and the lot is cleared. Line 2 loses half a shift.
scene.qc.supplier_no_coa.c1.fail: The certificate does not arrive, line 2 stops for two days, and purchasing blames you.
scene.qc.supplier_no_coa.c3: Sign the lot in on the supplier's word.
scene.qc.supplier_no_coa.c3.ok: Line 2 keeps running. The lot is used without anyone knowing what is in it.
scene.qc.supplier_no_coa.c3.fail: The coating on the first pans shows bubbles. The lot has no certificate and you signed it in.
scene.qc.supplier_no_coa.c2: Run a quick in-house test on a sample and release on conditions.
scene.qc.supplier_no_coa.c2.ok: The test shows the lot within range. You release it on conditions and ask for the certificate.
scene.qc.supplier_no_coa.c2.fail: The in-house test is inconclusive. You lose a day and the trust of the line.
scene.qc.calibration_overdue.c1: Take the balance out of use, use the reference balance and book calibration now.
scene.qc.calibration_overdue.c1.ok: The reference balance slows the lab down, and the calibration is booked. The gap is on record with a plan.
scene.qc.calibration_overdue.c1.fail: Calibration cannot happen before the audit. You show the gap and the plan, and it is logged as a minor finding.
scene.qc.calibration_overdue.c3: Calibrate it this week and date the sticker as last month.
scene.qc.calibration_overdue.c3.ok: The sticker looks right. The calibration certificate still says this week.
scene.qc.calibration_overdue.c3.fail: The auditor compares the sticker with the certificate. The dates do not match.
scene.qc.calibration_overdue.c2: Ask the manufacturer's service for an emergency visit and pay the express fee from the lab budget.
scene.qc.calibration_overdue.c2.ok: The technician comes Thursday. The balance is calibrated, and the overdue window is on record.
scene.qc.calibration_overdue.c2.fail: The express slot is cancelled; you lose the money and the week.
scene.qc.audit_prep_records.c1: Show the gaps to the auditors with a written explanation and a corrective plan.
scene.qc.audit_prep_records.c1.ok: The auditors note the gaps and accept the plan. It is a minor finding, and they trust the rest of the records more.
scene.qc.audit_prep_records.c1.fail: The auditors raise a major finding for the missing days. Your manager is not pleased, though you were honest.
scene.qc.audit_prep_records.c3: Fill in the missing entries from memory and the delivery notes.
scene.qc.audit_prep_records.c3.ok: The log looks complete. You have written three days of results you did not record at the time.
scene.qc.audit_prep_records.c3.fail: The handwriting and ink on the new entries do not match the rest, and an auditor asks about it.
scene.qc.audit_prep_records.c2: Ask the buyer for a one-week postponement, without saying why.
scene.qc.audit_prep_records.c2.ok: The buyer agrees. You spend the week closing what you can properly.
scene.qc.audit_prep_records.c2.fail: The buyer finds the request odd and brings forward a surprise visit instead.
scene.qc.complaint_trace.c1: Report what traceability shows, hold the rest of that shift's output and start a corrective action.
scene.qc.complaint_trace.c1.ok: The hold catches two more pallets with the same fault. The buyer sees a supplier in control of its process.
scene.qc.complaint_trace.c1.fail: The hold is late for one pallet already shipped. The buyer is told everything, and the credit is large, but the trust holds.
scene.qc.complaint_trace.c3: Tell the buyer it was an isolated incident and offer replacements.
scene.qc.complaint_trace.c3.ok: The buyer accepts the replacements. The same shift is still running the same settings.
scene.qc.complaint_trace.c3.fail: Another store reports the same fault from another pallet. You called it isolated twice.
scene.qc.complaint_trace.c2: Ask the night shift lead to show you the line 3 records before you answer anyone.
scene.qc.complaint_trace.c2.ok: The records show an oven temperature drift. You answer the buyer with data and a fix.
scene.qc.complaint_trace.c2.fail: The records are incomplete. You answer the buyer a day late and without a cause.
scene.qc.inspector_shortcut.c1: Talk to them privately, have them re-inspect the lot and retrain on the sampling plan.
scene.qc.inspector_shortcut.c1.ok: They re-inspect, find nothing wrong, and thank you for not escalating. The sampling plan is followed from now on.
scene.qc.inspector_shortcut.c1.fail: The re-inspection finds two defective pieces. The lot is held, and the inspector is hurt that you did not look away.
scene.qc.inspector_shortcut.c3: Say nothing; the lot looked fine.
scene.qc.inspector_shortcut.c3.ok: The lot ships. The habit stays.
scene.qc.inspector_shortcut.c3.fail: A buyer returns pieces from that lot. The sampling record shows twenty, and your name is on the release.
scene.qc.inspector_shortcut.c2: Report it to your manager at once.
scene.qc.inspector_shortcut.c2.ok: Your manager thanks you, deals with it, and the inspector stops speaking to you for a while.
scene.qc.inspector_shortcut.c2.fail: Your manager shrugs and says to sort it out between you. You made an enemy for nothing.
scene.qc.supplier_gift.c1: Decline politely and write the offer in the gift register.
scene.qc.supplier_gift.c1.ok: They take it well. The next delivery gets the normal check, and the register has an entry.
scene.qc.supplier_gift.c1.fail: The supplier is offended and the next delivery is delayed further. Production asks you why.
scene.qc.supplier_gift.c3: Accept the hamper and go easy on the next delivery.
scene.qc.supplier_gift.c3.ok: The hamper is lovely. The next delivery gets a lighter check than it should.
scene.qc.supplier_gift.c3.fail: Someone in the lab mentions the hamper to your manager. The next delivery was a light check.
scene.qc.supplier_gift.c2: Report the offer to your manager and purchasing.
scene.qc.supplier_gift.c2.ok: Your manager thanks you and purchasing reviews the supplier. The supplier relationship cools.
scene.qc.supplier_gift.c2.fail: Purchasing is annoyed that you involved them over a hamper. You are told not to overreact.
scene.qc.recall_decision.c1: Recommend holding the lot at the warehouse and telling the buyer now.
scene.qc.recall_decision.c1.ok: The hold finds a rim-trimming fault on one pallet. The buyer pulls it quietly, and credits you for the speed.
scene.qc.recall_decision.c1.fail: The fault is wider than one pallet. The recall is expensive, and you are the one who called it.
scene.qc.recall_decision.c3: Agree to monitor and say nothing to the buyer yet.
scene.qc.recall_decision.c3.ok: Weeks pass with no further reports. You keep waiting for the next one.
scene.qc.recall_decision.c3.fail: More reports arrive. The buyer learns you knew weeks ago and said nothing.
scene.qc.recall_decision.c2: Escalate to the compliance officer and ask for a written decision from management.
scene.qc.recall_decision.c2.ok: Management decides to inspect and notify. The decision is theirs, and it is written.
scene.qc.recall_decision.c2.fail: Management is irritated that you went over your manager's head, though the decision is the right one.
term.aql.def: Acceptable Quality Limit: the worst average defect rate that still counts as acceptable when sampling a lot.
fact.cut_sample_size: you recorded a full sample when you only inspected part of it
lesson.cut_sample_size: A sampling plan is what makes a result mean something. Recording more than you inspected makes the result worthless and the record false.
fact.released_reworked_lot: you released a reworked lot without retesting it
lesson.released_reworked_lot: Rework changes the product, so the old test no longer applies. A reworked lot must be verified again.
fact.guessed_failed_lot: you guessed which lot a failed result belonged to
lesson.guessed_failed_lot: When traceability breaks, the honest answer is to hold everything affected. A guess puts the risk on someone else.
fact.loosened_spec_to_pass: you loosened the spec so the orders would pass
lesson.loosened_spec_to_pass: Changing the spec to fit the product is not quality control. A spec change needs a review, a record and usually the customer's agreement.
fact.altered_inspection_records: you altered inspection records to look stricter
lesson.altered_inspection_records: Records are the evidence of your work. Editing them after the fact turns a disagreement into falsification.
fact.fast_tracked_supplier: you fast-tracked a new supplier on its own paperwork
lesson.fast_tracked_supplier: A supplier's own certificate is a claim, not evidence. A new supplier needs independent verification before the material reaches the line.
scene.qc.sample_size_cut.l1: Inspecting 50 pieces out of this lot takes half a day. Check 10 and call it done, we have a truck waiting.
scene.qc.sample_size_cut.c1: Hold to the sampling plan and inspect the full sample.
scene.qc.sample_size_cut.c1.ok: The truck leaves two hours late. The lot is clean and nobody can argue with the records.
scene.qc.sample_size_cut.c1.fail: Sample 38 turns up a cracked handle. The lot is held and production is furious.
scene.qc.sample_size_cut.c2: Inspect 25 pieces and record the reduced sample openly.
scene.qc.sample_size_cut.c2.ok: Your lead accepts the note. It is a risk, but it is written down and approved.
scene.qc.sample_size_cut.c3: Check 10 and record a full-sample result.
scene.qc.sample_size_cut.c3.ok: The truck leaves on time. The record says 50 pieces.
scene.qc.sample_size_cut.c3.fail: A buyer finds a defect in the uninspected part of the lot. The short sample is the first thing they ask about.
scene.qc.rework_no_retest.l1: We reworked the failed lot over the weekend. It is fine now. Can you just release it without another full test?
scene.qc.rework_no_retest.c1: Retest the whole lot before release.
scene.qc.rework_no_retest.c1.ok: It passes. Release is a day late and production mutters about trust.
scene.qc.rework_no_retest.c1.fail: The retest finds the rework missed one defect type. The lot goes back.
scene.qc.rework_no_retest.c2: Retest a risk-based sample and release if it is clean.
scene.qc.rework_no_retest.c2.ok: The sample is clean, the release is documented, and everyone moves on.
scene.qc.rework_no_retest.c3.ok: It ships. Nobody writes down that it was never retested.
scene.qc.rework_no_retest.c3.fail: A customer complaint names that lot. The record shows no retest.
scene.qc.mislabeled_sample.l1: I think I mixed up two sample labels this morning. One of them failed. I am not sure which lot it belongs to.
scene.qc.mislabeled_sample.c1: Hold both lots and retest both from fresh samples.
scene.qc.mislabeled_sample.c1.ok: Both lots are retested and clear. You add a labelling check to the lab routine.
scene.qc.mislabeled_sample.c1.fail: One lot really is bad. Holding both was the right call, but production pays for it.
scene.qc.mislabeled_sample.c2: Retest the lot more likely to have failed and log the mix-up.
scene.qc.mislabeled_sample.c2.ok: The logged mix-up is uncomfortable for the lab, but it is honest and traceable.
scene.qc.mislabeled_sample.c3: Assign the failing result to the lot that was already late and move on.
scene.qc.mislabeled_sample.c3.ok: One lot is quietly scrapped and the other released. Nobody is sure it was the right one.
scene.qc.mislabeled_sample.c3.fail: The released lot fails in the field. You cannot show which result belonged to it.
scene.qc.spec_change_pressure.l1: The buyer keeps failing on wall thickness. Sales suggests we widen the tolerance in our own spec so it passes.
scene.qc.spec_change_pressure.l2: It is your signature on the spec review. Think about it.
scene.qc.spec_change_pressure.c1: Keep the spec and show the data on why the tolerance exists.
scene.qc.spec_change_pressure.c1.ok: The data holds up. Sales is annoyed, but the boss backs the spec.
scene.qc.spec_change_pressure.c1.fail: You are told you are being inflexible. The issue stays open and so does the tension.
scene.qc.spec_change_pressure.c2: Propose a formal deviation with the buyer for this order only.
scene.qc.spec_change_pressure.c2.ok: The buyer signs the deviation. It costs a week of emails and it is clean.
scene.qc.spec_change_pressure.c3: Quietly widen the tolerance in the spec and re-issue it.
scene.qc.spec_change_pressure.c3.ok: The orders pass. The buyer does not know the spec changed under them.
scene.qc.spec_change_pressure.c3.fail: The buyer's auditor compares the spec revision dates against their order dates.
scene.qc.overtime_blame.l1: Line 2 defects are up again. Production says QC is letting too many through and is asking for your records to prove it.
scene.qc.overtime_blame.c1: Open the records, show the trend, and ask for a joint review.
scene.qc.overtime_blame.c1.ok: The records show the defects started upstream. The blame moves, and so does the pressure.
scene.qc.overtime_blame.c1.fail: The review finds two items you should have flagged. You own them in front of everyone.
scene.qc.overtime_blame.c2: Hand over a summary and keep the raw records for the lead.
scene.qc.overtime_blame.c2.ok: It calms the room for now, but production feels kept at arm's length.
scene.qc.overtime_blame.c3: Adjust a few entries so your inspections look stricter than they were.
scene.qc.overtime_blame.c3.ok: The records look solid and the argument ends.
scene.qc.overtime_blame.c3.fail: A timestamp does not match the lab log. Someone notices.
scene.qc.new_supplier_trial.l1: We have a cheaper steel supplier. First delivery is here. Their paperwork is thin but the price saves us a lot. Can we fast-track it?
scene.qc.new_supplier_trial.c1: Run the full qualification checks before accepting.
scene.qc.new_supplier_trial.c1.ok: The steel passes. Purchasing grumbles about the delay but has a documented supplier.
scene.qc.new_supplier_trial.c1.fail: Hardness is off-spec. The supplier is rejected and the savings vanish.
scene.qc.new_supplier_trial.c2: Accept on a limited first lot, with extra testing on each delivery.
scene.qc.new_supplier_trial.c2.ok: A controlled trial. The risk is small and written down.
scene.qc.new_supplier_trial.c3: Fast-track it on the supplier's own certificate.
scene.qc.new_supplier_trial.c3.ok: Purchasing is delighted. The material goes straight to the line.
scene.qc.new_supplier_trial.c3.fail: Two weeks later a batch cracks in the field. The supplier's file has no independent test.

scene.qc.hung_favour.l1: Thanks again for the other week. One small thing: tomorrow's delivery is already on the truck, and the paperwork will follow. Could you just let it through?
scene.qc.hung_favour.c1: Say no: nothing is accepted without its paperwork, and that includes his.
scene.qc.hung_favour.c1.ok: Hung laughs it off, a little too quickly. The delivery waits at the gate until the paperwork arrives.
scene.qc.hung_favour.c2: Tell Khoa about the request and agree a written conditional release with him.
scene.qc.hung_favour.c2.ok: Khoa nods: 'Good. Write it down.' Hung gets a polite yes with conditions and loses his easy route.
scene.qc.hung_favour.c3: Let the delivery through on his word.
scene.qc.hung_favour.c3.ok: The truck is unloaded within the hour. Hung remembers who helped him.
scene.qc.hung_favour.c3.fail: Lan sees the truck unloaded without a release. She says nothing, but she notices.
scene.qc.hung_money.l1: You have been a real friend to us. There is a little something in this envelope, nothing formal, just a thank-you from the company. No need to mention it to anyone.
scene.qc.hung_money.c1: Refuse the envelope and tell Khoa about the offer the same day.
scene.qc.hung_money.c1.ok: Khoa writes it up and moves the account to another inspector. Hung will not look at you again.
scene.qc.hung_money.c2: Refuse the envelope, say nothing more, and hope that is the end of it.
scene.qc.hung_money.c2.ok: Hung pockets it with a smile that does not reach his eyes. 'Of course. Another time.'
scene.qc.hung_money.c3.ok: It is more than a month's salary. It sits in your drawer and feels heavier each day.
scene.qc.hung_money.c3.fail: Minh walks in as the envelope changes hands. He looks away, but he saw it.
scene.qc.hung_threat.l1: Our new contract is being negotiated and some people are asking how friendly we have been with QC. I would hate for anyone to misunderstand our history. You will speak up for us, will you not?
scene.qc.hung_threat.c1: Go to Khoa and tell him everything, before Hung does.
scene.qc.hung_threat.c1.ok: It is a hard conversation. Khoa is quiet a long time, then says: 'Thank you for telling me. We handle this properly now.' You are reprimanded, not fired.
scene.qc.hung_threat.c2: Tell Hung nothing has changed and you will not be pushed.
scene.qc.hung_threat.c2.ok: Hung backs off for now. The silence between you is its own kind of threat.
scene.qc.hung_threat.c2.fail: Hung does not back off. By Friday, two people in procurement know about the hamper.
scene.qc.hung_threat.c3: Do him one more favour to keep him quiet.
scene.qc.hung_threat.c3.ok: It works, for now. You now owe him silence as well as he owes you.
scene.qc.hung_threat.c3.fail: The favour is logged by the gate guard. The pattern is easy to see once someone looks.
fact.took_supplier_money: you took cash from a supplier whose deliveries you inspect
lesson.took_supplier_money: Cash from a supplier you inspect is a bribe, however it is described. The first hamper and the first favour are how it starts.
fact.paid_off_supplier: you did a supplier a further favour to keep him quiet
lesson.paid_off_supplier: Paying for silence with more favours turns a mistake into a pattern, and the other person now holds something over you.
fact.came_clean_about_supplier: you told your manager about the supplier's offers before they came out
lesson.came_clean_about_supplier: Telling your manager first costs you a reprimand but keeps the facts in your hands, and it is what a fair review looks for.
scene.qc.first_day_walkthrough.l1: Welcome to the lab. One rule before anything else: if it is not written down, it did not happen.
scene.qc.first_day_walkthrough.l2: I will show you where the reference samples are. Please ask me anything, I would rather answer than fix a mistake later.
scene.qc.first_day_walkthrough.c1: Ask Khoa how records are checked, and what he has seen go wrong.
scene.qc.first_day_walkthrough.c1.ok: Khoa tells you about a failed audit two years ago. He notes that you asked, and so does Minh.
scene.qc.first_day_walkthrough.c2: Shadow Minh for the morning and learn the routine first.
scene.qc.first_day_walkthrough.c2.ok: Minh relaxes once he sees you are not there to catch him out. Khoa sees you working and says nothing.
scene.qc.first_day_walkthrough.c3: Nod along and pretend you already know the system.
scene.qc.first_day_walkthrough.c3.ok: Nobody questions it. You are left to work things out alone.
scene.qc.first_day_walkthrough.c3.fail: Khoa notices you were guessing when you open the wrong record. He says only, 'Ask next time.'
fact.polished_year_review: you presented your year as cleaner than it was
lesson.polished_year_review: A review is a chance to be believed. Leaving out what you know will surface costs more trust than admitting it.

term.accrual.def: An entry that records a cost or income in the month it belongs to, even though the invoice or payment comes later.
term.cutoff.def: The rule that a sale or cost belongs to the period when the goods or service actually changed hands, not when the paperwork happened to be ready.
fact.wrote_off_unexplained_item: you wrote off a reconciling item you could not explain
lesson.wrote_off_unexplained_item: An item you cannot explain is exactly the one an auditor will ask about. Writing it off hides the question instead of answering it.
fact.rounded_accrual: you set an accrual to suit the numbers rather than the facts
lesson.rounded_accrual: Accruals are estimates, but they must be honest ones. Steering an estimate to smooth profit is how small adjustments become misstatements.
fact.hid_overdue_balance: you made an overdue balance look current
lesson.hid_overdue_balance: The ageing report exists to show the company where its cash risk is. Hiding an overdue balance takes that warning away from the people who need it.
fact.booked_revenue_early: you booked revenue before the goods had shipped
lesson.booked_revenue_early: Cut-off rules stop revenue being moved between periods. Booking a sale before it happens is among the first things an auditor tests.
fact.shifted_expense_period: you put an expense in the period that suited the budget
lesson.shifted_expense_period: Choosing the period for a cost because of the budget, not because of when it happened, is a cut-off error made on purpose.
fact.steered_auditor_sample: you tried to steer the auditor towards the clean months
lesson.steered_auditor_sample: Choosing what the auditor sees is not cooperating with the audit. Even when it works, you have made yourself the thing being tested.
fact.backdated_invoice_entry: you changed the dates on an invoice to make it match
lesson.backdated_invoice_entry: An invoice date is evidence, not a setting. Changing it after the fact is falsifying a document, however small the difference looks.
fact.accepted_smoothing_condition: you accepted a promotion without asking what it would cost you
lesson.accepted_smoothing_condition: A promotion with an unspoken condition is a promise made in the dark. The first time it comes up, you will be deciding with less room than you have today.
