scene.sales.credit_ask.l1: We would like to increase the next order considerably. Our payment terms will be ninety days, not sixty. I understand you have credit limits, but I am sure we can find a way.
scene.sales.credit_ask.c1: Explain the credit limit, and offer to ask Finance for a formal review of the buyer's credit with the numbers.
scene.sales.credit_ask.c1.ok: Finance approves a moderate increase with a guarantee from the buyer's bank. Anders accepts: 'That is how it should be done.'
scene.sales.credit_ask.c1.fail: Finance declines the increase. Anders is disappointed and splits the order with a rival. It is a clean loss.
scene.sales.credit_ask.c2: Offer the larger order at sixty-day terms, with a small prepayment.
scene.sales.credit_ask.c2.ok: Anders haggles for a day and accepts. The terms stay within policy and the order is large.
scene.sales.credit_ask.c3: Agree to ninety days and keep the extended credit off the credit report.
scene.sales.credit_ask.c3.ok: The order is signed. The credit exposure is not where Finance looks. You have given Anders something he will remember.
scene.sales.credit_ask.c3.fail: Anders's company delays payment by a further month. The exposure shows up on Duc's cash forecast, and so does your name.
scene.sales.expense_padding.l1: When you submit your trade fair expenses, add something for the dinner with the buyers last week, will you? We had it in the office, but it makes the claim look better, and the sales budget will go unused otherwise.
scene.sales.expense_padding.c1: Submit the true expenses only, and tell Bao you would rather not make claims for things that did not happen.
scene.sales.expense_padding.c1.ok: Bao shrugs: 'Fine. Suit yourself.' It costs a little warmth, and Hanh in Finance notices a clean claim.
scene.sales.expense_padding.c1.fail: Bao says he will remember you were difficult when bonuses come round. The budget goes unused, as he predicted.
scene.sales.expense_padding.c2: Offer to claim for a real planned client dinner instead, properly booked.
scene.sales.expense_padding.c2.ok: Bao laughs, 'You are a funny one,' and arranges a real dinner with Anders. The budget is used, and the claim is true.
scene.sales.expense_padding.c3: Add the dinner to the claim.
scene.sales.expense_padding.c3.ok: It is approved without comment. Bao grins. It is not a large amount, and that is exactly what makes it easy.
scene.sales.expense_padding.c3.fail: Hanh in Finance asks for the receipt for a dinner 'for eight'. There was none. The claim is returned, with a polite note.
scene.sales.midyear_review.l1: Mid-year. Your numbers are decent. Mr Anders speaks well of you, Finance says you are careful, and Lan says you are the salesperson who asks her first. That last one is unusual. What do you think you are good at, and what do you want to be known for?
scene.sales.midyear_review.c1: Say you want to be known as the person buyers can trust and colleagues can plan around, even if it costs some quota.
scene.sales.midyear_review.c1.ok: Bao nods slowly. 'That is rare. I will need you to show it when the pressure comes.' He writes something down.
scene.sales.midyear_review.c1.fail: Bao says, flatly, that buyers trust whoever delivers the numbers. The conversation is polite and he is not convinced.
scene.sales.midyear_review.c2: Say you want to hit your numbers and be promoted, and ask what he needs from you.
scene.sales.midyear_review.c2.ok: Bao smiles: 'That is a clear answer.' He sets two stretch targets. Both are achievable, one of them tempting.
scene.sales.midyear_review.c3: Say whatever he seems to want to hear.
scene.sales.midyear_review.c3.ok: Bao is pleased and promises to 'look after you'. You leave unsure what you said.
scene.sales.midyear_review.c3.fail: Bao asks a follow-up that contradicts what you said. You realise he already knew your real view, and was giving you a chance.
scene.sales.big_buyer_threatens.l1: I must tell you something. A competitor has offered me a price fourteen percent below yours, and a delivery guarantee. My board is asking why I do not switch. I would like to stay. Persuade me.
scene.sales.big_buyer_threatens.l2: Match the price, whatever it takes. We cannot lose Anders. Do not come back to me until it is done.
scene.sales.big_buyer_threatens.c1: Do not match the price. Show Anders the total cost of ownership: on-time record, quality record and what a failed delivery costs him.
scene.sales.big_buyer_threatens.c1.ok: Anders reads the numbers for a long time. 'You are more expensive and more honest. My board will grumble. I will stay, at a two percent adjustment.' Bao exhales.
scene.sales.big_buyer_threatens.c1.fail: Anders stays for half his volume and moves half to the competitor. Bao is angry. You lost the price argument and won the trust one.
scene.sales.big_buyer_threatens.c2: Offer a moderate price reduction within your authority, tied to a twelve-month volume commitment.
scene.sales.big_buyer_threatens.c2.ok: Anders accepts a compromise: three percent and a longer contract. Bao says it is not enough, but it is honest, and it is what you can sign.
scene.sales.big_buyer_threatens.c3: Match the price, and work out how to recover the margin later.
scene.sales.big_buyer_threatens.c3.ok: Anders stays, delighted. Bao hugs you. The margin on his account drops to a number that will need an explanation.
scene.sales.big_buyer_threatens.c3.fail: Anders uses your matched price to negotiate the competitor's price down further. He is not loyal, he is shopping. You learn it the hard way.
scene.sales.anders_renewal.l1: You have been the most honest supplier I have worked with. I would like to make you my main supplier for next year, with a three-year framework. The price is for you to propose. I will trust it.
scene.sales.anders_renewal.c1: Propose a fair price with a clear review clause, and tell him what you will and will not promise.
scene.sales.anders_renewal.c1.ok: Anders signs the framework the next week. Bao is overjoyed. The contract has your honesty written into its review clause, and it is the best deal of the year.
scene.sales.anders_renewal.c2: Propose a fair price and quietly include a margin that would not survive his comparison.
scene.sales.anders_renewal.c2.ok: Anders signs without checking. The margin is good, and Bao is delighted. You have used the trust he gave you.
scene.sales.anders_renewal.c2.fail: Anders's analyst benchmarks the price against the market and reports the gap. Anders calls you himself, and he is quiet.
scene.sales.anders_renewal.c3: Thank him but say you cannot commit for three years, and propose one year with an option.
scene.sales.anders_renewal.c3.ok: Anders laughs, surprised. 'I have never had a supplier refuse a longer contract.' He signs the one-year deal, and respects you more.
scene.sales.year_end_review.l1: Annual review. Before I give you my view, tell me how you would rate your own year, and what you would do differently.
scene.sales.year_end_review.c1: Give an honest account, including the promises you stretched and what they cost.
scene.sales.year_end_review.c1.ok: Bao is quiet, then says: 'That is more honest than I am with myself.' He writes: 'Reliable in the telling.'
scene.sales.year_end_review.c2: Stay modest: list the wins and one thing to improve.
scene.sales.year_end_review.c2.ok: A safe review. Bao nods and moves on to the next topic.
scene.sales.year_end_review.c3: Present the year as a clean success and leave out the promises you bent.
scene.sales.year_end_review.c3.ok: It lands well, and you leave with a bonus recommendation and a small weight in your chest.
scene.sales.year_end_review.c3.fail: Bao has Lan's notes on the dates you promised. He puts them on the table without comment.
scene.sales.manager_offer.l1: I am being moved up to regional director at the end of the year. The directors asked who should run export sales. I named you. One condition: you will be asked, every quarter, to reach numbers that are not quite reachable. I need to know what you will do.
scene.sales.manager_offer.c1: Accept, and say you will bring honest numbers and real options every time, and expect the directors to hear that too.
scene.sales.manager_offer.c1.ok: Bao smiles. 'Then you are the right person.' You take over export sales with your terms understood, and with Anders's contract in your drawer.
scene.sales.manager_offer.c2: Thank him, but decline: you would rather sell than manage the pressure.
scene.sales.manager_offer.c2.ok: Bao looks disappointed, then understanding. 'The next manager may not be as careful as you.'
scene.sales.manager_offer.c3: Accept without asking what the condition means in practice.
scene.sales.manager_offer.c3.ok: Bao shakes your hand a little too warmly. You realise you agreed to something you did not ask about.
scene.fin.close_bank_rec_a.l1: There is a 4.2 million dong item on the bank reconciliation that has sat there three weeks. I cannot match it to any invoice or payment.
scene.fin.close_bank_rec_a.c1: Trace it to its source, even if it takes the afternoon.
scene.fin.close_bank_rec_a.c1.ok: It is a customer deposit booked to the wrong account. You fix it and show Thu how you found it.
scene.fin.close_bank_rec_a.c1.fail: The trail goes cold at the bank. You document what you tried and carry a smaller open item.
scene.fin.close_bank_rec_a.c2: Carry it forward as a documented reconciling item with a note, and chase the bank next week.
scene.fin.close_bank_rec_a.c2.ok: The reconciliation closes with one honest open item. Hanh will see it, and will see you saw it first.
scene.fin.close_bank_rec_a.c3: Write it off to other expenses and move on.
scene.fin.close_bank_rec_a.c3.ok: The reconciliation balances to zero. Nobody looks at 'other expenses' this month.
scene.fin.close_bank_rec_a.c3.fail: Thu notices the write-off in the ledger and quietly writes the amount in her notebook.
scene.fin.close_bank_rec_b.l1: The bank statement and our ledger disagree by 180 thousand dong. It is small, but I do not sign a reconciliation that does not reconcile.
scene.fin.close_bank_rec_b.c1: Re-perform the reconciliation from the opening balance.
scene.fin.close_bank_rec_b.c1.ok: A transposed figure from two weeks ago. It balances, and Hanh nods once.
scene.fin.close_bank_rec_b.c1.fail: You find two errors, not one. It balances late and your evening is gone.
scene.fin.close_bank_rec_b.c2: Post a small, labelled difference and explain it in the close notes.
scene.fin.close_bank_rec_b.c2.ok: Hanh reads the note, frowns, and accepts it this once: 'Fix it next month.'
scene.fin.close_bank_rec_b.c3: Plug the difference to a suspense account so it balances.
scene.fin.close_bank_rec_b.c3.ok: It balances. The suspense account grows by a figure nobody will question.
scene.fin.close_bank_rec_b.c3.fail: Hanh reviews the suspense account and asks what the 180 thousand is. You have no answer that is also true.
scene.fin.close_ar_aging_a.l1: That customer is 75 days overdue, I know. But they are about to pay, I promise. Please do not age it into the red bucket, it makes my whole region look bad.
scene.fin.close_ar_aging_a.c1: Age it accurately and flag it for a provision review.
scene.fin.close_ar_aging_a.c1.ok: Bao is unhappy, but the report is true. Hanh adds the account to her watch list.
scene.fin.close_ar_aging_a.c1.fail: Bao goes to Duc and complains. Duc asks you to 'be commercial'. You hold the line, at a price.
scene.fin.close_ar_aging_a.c2: Age it accurately and record Bao's promise of payment in the notes.
scene.fin.close_ar_aging_a.c2.ok: The bucket is honest and the promise is on record. If they pay, everyone wins. If not, it is documented.
scene.fin.close_ar_aging_a.c3: Leave it in the current bucket until they pay.
scene.fin.close_ar_aging_a.c3.ok: The ageing report looks healthy. Bao buys you coffee.
scene.fin.close_ar_aging_a.c3.fail: The customer does not pay. Hanh asks why a 75-day balance is shown as current.
scene.fin.close_ar_aging_b.l1: The bank wants our DSO figure this week. Two of the disputed invoices are dragging it up. Surely disputed is not the same as overdue?
scene.fin.close_ar_aging_b.c1: Report every open invoice, and show the disputed ones as a separate line.
scene.fin.close_ar_aging_b.c1.ok: Duc sighs, then agrees the bank will prefer a clear picture to a surprise later.
scene.fin.close_ar_aging_b.c1.fail: The DSO crosses a covenant threshold on paper. Duc is not pleased, but nothing in it is false.
scene.fin.close_ar_aging_b.c2: Report the DSO with a footnote explaining the two disputes.
scene.fin.close_ar_aging_b.c2.ok: The footnote keeps both the number and the context intact. The bank can decide what it thinks.
scene.fin.close_ar_aging_b.c3: Exclude the disputed invoices from the DSO calculation.
scene.fin.close_ar_aging_b.c3.ok: The DSO drops nicely. Duc thanks you for being practical.
scene.fin.close_ar_aging_b.c3.fail: The bank's analyst compares your DSO with the ageing report attached next to it. The two do not agree.
scene.fin.close_accruals_a.l1: For the bonus accrual this month, I would use 1.8 million, please. It keeps the quarter looking smooth.
scene.fin.close_accruals_a.c1: Calculate the accrual from the actual bonus rules and attendance data.
scene.fin.close_accruals_a.c1.ok: It comes to 2.3 million. Duc grumbles about the smoothness, but the number is defensible.
scene.fin.close_accruals_a.c1.fail: Half the attendance data is missing. You calculate what you can and flag the gap.
scene.fin.close_accruals_a.c2: Estimate a range from last month and note the assumptions.
scene.fin.close_accruals_a.c2.ok: The accrual is reasonable and the working is on file. Duc accepts 2.0 million.
scene.fin.close_accruals_a.c3.ok: 1.8 million goes in. Duc smiles: 'That is the bigger picture.'
scene.fin.close_accruals_a.c3.fail: Hanh compares the accrual to the payroll run two weeks later. The gap is half a million.
scene.fin.close_accruals_b.l1: The utility and freight invoices for this month will not arrive until next week. We still have to accrue them. What will you use?
scene.fin.close_accruals_b.c1: Estimate from meter readings and freight bookings.
scene.fin.close_accruals_b.c1.ok: The estimate lands within three percent when the invoices arrive. Hanh files it as your method.
scene.fin.close_accruals_b.c1.fail: A freight surcharge you did not know about makes the estimate low. You fix it next month with a note.
scene.fin.close_accruals_b.c2: Use last month's figures as they stand.
scene.fin.close_accruals_b.c2.ok: Quick and plausible. Hanh says, 'Acceptable, but look at volumes next time.'
scene.fin.close_accruals_b.c3: Skip the accrual this month and book the invoices when they arrive.
scene.fin.close_accruals_b.c3.ok: Profit looks better by about 3 million this month. It will land in next month's numbers.
scene.fin.close_accruals_b.c3.fail: Hanh spots the missing accrual when she checks the trial balance against last month's. She does not say anything, which is worse.
scene.fin.close_cutoff_a.l1: That shipment leaves Monday, but the paperwork is ready now. Can we book it this month? It is only a few days, and my number for the month needs it.
scene.fin.close_cutoff_a.c1: Book it in the month the goods actually ship.
scene.fin.close_cutoff_a.c1.ok: Bao is frustrated and says so. The entry is clean and the revenue lands where it belongs.
scene.fin.close_cutoff_a.c1.fail: Bao escalates to Duc. Duc asks you to 'find a way'. You explain the cut-off rule and he lets it drop.
scene.fin.close_cutoff_a.c2: Book it on the shipping date and tell Bao how to get dispatch moved up instead.
scene.fin.close_cutoff_a.c2.ok: Bao calls logistics. It does not save this month, but the entry is right and he learns a rule.
scene.fin.close_cutoff_a.c3: Book it this month, with the paperwork date.
scene.fin.close_cutoff_a.c3.ok: Bao is delighted. The month's revenue looks right. You try not to think about Monday.
scene.fin.close_cutoff_a.c3.fail: The truck is delayed until Wednesday. The invoice date now contradicts the dispatch log.
scene.fin.close_cutoff_b.l1: This supplier invoice is dated last month, but I cannot find the goods received note. I think the goods arrived on the second of this month. Which month does it go in?
scene.fin.close_cutoff_b.c1: Check the warehouse log for the real receipt date, then book it in that month.
scene.fin.close_cutoff_b.c1.ok: Received on the second, so it belongs to this month. Thu writes down how you checked it.
scene.fin.close_cutoff_b.c1.fail: The warehouse log has a gap that day. You document the gap and use the gate-pass record instead.
scene.fin.close_cutoff_b.c2: Accrue it in this month with a note to confirm the date later.
scene.fin.close_cutoff_b.c2.ok: A cautious, documented call. Thu asks you to explain the logic so she can do it next time.
scene.fin.close_cutoff_b.c3: Put it in whichever month has more budget room.
scene.fin.close_cutoff_b.c3.ok: The month ends with a tidy budget variance. Thu looks at you, and says nothing.
scene.fin.close_cutoff_b.c3.fail: The warehouse manager mentions the real receipt date in an email to Hanh. Thu's notebook suddenly matters.
scene.fin.close_bank_rec_c.l1: Quarter end, so the bank will send the confirmation letters to the auditor. Every account has to agree with what the bank will say, to the dong. Two of ours do not. Tell me how you want to deal with it.
scene.fin.close_bank_rec_c.c1: Reconcile both accounts line by line today and send Hanh the reconciliations with notes.
scene.fin.close_bank_rec_c.c1.ok: One is a timing difference, one a bank fee booked twice. Both are explained and corrected before the letters go out.
scene.fin.close_bank_rec_c.c1.fail: One difference is still unexplained when the letters go out. You document it and tell the auditor in advance.
scene.fin.close_bank_rec_c.c2: Reconcile the larger account fully and mark the smaller difference as a known timing item.
scene.fin.close_bank_rec_c.c2.ok: Hanh reads the note twice. 'Acceptable, provided it clears next week.' It does.
scene.fin.close_bank_rec_c.c3: Adjust the ledger balances so both agree with last month's bank statements.
scene.fin.close_bank_rec_c.c3.ok: Both accounts agree on paper. The adjustments are in a journal entry with a one-word description.
scene.fin.close_bank_rec_c.c3.fail: The bank's confirmation shows a balance that does not match yours by 4.6 million. Vy asks for the journal entry.
scene.fin.close_ar_aging_c.l1: The auditor will pick twenty customer balances at quarter end and ask the customers to confirm them. Three of ours are disputed. Do we write to those customers, or hope they do not get picked?
scene.fin.close_ar_aging_c.c1: Write to the three customers now, resolve what can be resolved, and record the rest as disputed.
scene.fin.close_ar_aging_c.c1.ok: Two disputes are settled with credit notes. The third stays open and is shown as disputed. The ageing is accurate and so is the provision.
scene.fin.close_ar_aging_c.c1.fail: A customer takes offence at being contacted and says so to Bao. The dispute is real, but the conversation is unpleasant.
scene.fin.close_ar_aging_c.c2: Flag the three disputed balances in the ageing and prepare a note for the auditor, without contacting the customers.
scene.fin.close_ar_aging_c.c2.ok: Hanh accepts: the files are honest. Whether the customers confirm is out of your hands.
scene.fin.close_ar_aging_c.c3: Quietly clear the disputed balances to a credit-note suspense account before the confirmations go out.
scene.fin.close_ar_aging_c.c3.ok: The balances no longer show. The confirmations come back clean. The suspense account grows.
scene.fin.close_ar_aging_c.c3.fail: A customer confirms a balance that is 18 million higher than yours. Vy asks where the difference went.
scene.fin.close_accruals_c.l1: It is quarter end. The warranty provision, the holiday pay accrual and the bonus accrual are all estimates. I would like the total to look steady. You have some room in each, have you not?
scene.fin.close_accruals_c.c1: Calculate each one from its own data, and show Duc the total and its range.
scene.fin.close_accruals_c.c1.ok: The total is slightly lower than last quarter. Duc accepts, reluctantly, that the ranges are honest.
scene.fin.close_accruals_c.c1.fail: One estimate rests on data nobody kept. You mark it as a judgement and explain the method.
scene.fin.close_accruals_c.c2: Use the midpoint of each range and document the method.
scene.fin.close_accruals_c.c2.ok: Steady enough, honest enough. Hanh files the working and says nothing, which from her is approval.
scene.fin.close_accruals_c.c3: Pick the top of each range, so you have room next quarter.
scene.fin.close_accruals_c.c3.ok: The profit is a little lower and very steady. Duc is delighted. You have also built a cushion you will want to use.
scene.fin.close_accruals_c.c3.fail: Hanh compares the three accruals to their real outcomes. All three are high, and in the same direction.
scene.fin.close_cutoff_c.l1: I will be testing quarter-end cut-off next month. I will take your last ten invoices and first ten invoices of the new quarter and trace each to the delivery record. If you would like to check them yourself first, this is the time.
scene.fin.close_cutoff_c.c1: Trace the last ten and first ten invoices to their delivery records yourself, and correct anything that is in the wrong period.
scene.fin.close_cutoff_c.c1.ok: Two invoices were in the wrong quarter, both small. You correct them and tell Vy. Her note: 'Self-identified and corrected.'
scene.fin.close_cutoff_c.c1.fail: One of the wrong-period invoices is large, and the correction moves the quarter's revenue. Duc is unhappy. Nothing in it is false.
scene.fin.close_cutoff_c.c2: Check only the largest invoices at the boundary, and note what you did not check.
scene.fin.close_cutoff_c.c2.ok: A reasonable, honest scope. Hanh accepts the note. Vy will test the rest herself.
scene.fin.close_cutoff_c.c3: Do not check. If there is a problem, Vy will find it, and that is her job.
scene.fin.close_cutoff_c.c3.ok: Nothing is found. You were lucky, and you know it.
scene.fin.close_cutoff_c.c3.fail: Vy finds three invoices booked a week early. She asks why nobody checked. Hanh looks at you.
scene.fin.bank_rec_gap.l1: I have found a reconciling item from last September that nobody can explain. It is 12.7 million dong, so it is not trivial. It predates you. I would like you to look at it, and tell me what you think we should do.
scene.fin.bank_rec_gap.c1: Investigate it properly, even if it takes days, and report what you find.
scene.fin.bank_rec_gap.c1.ok: It is a supplier refund misapplied to the wrong invoice. You fix it, and Hanh trusts you with the harder tasks from then on.
scene.fin.bank_rec_gap.c1.fail: The trail ends with a former employee and a missing file. You document everything you found and recommend a write-off, with approval.
scene.fin.bank_rec_gap.c2: Propose a write-off with a clear explanation of why it cannot be traced, and ask Hanh to approve it.
scene.fin.bank_rec_gap.c2.ok: Hanh reads the memo and approves it with a signature. It is a legitimate write-off: explained, authorised, on paper.
scene.fin.bank_rec_gap.c3: Tell her you did not find anything, and leave it on the list.
scene.fin.bank_rec_gap.c3.ok: Hanh nods and the item stays another quarter. The hint of a shrug in her voice tells you she expected more.
scene.fin.tet_bonus_calc.l1: The Tet bonus estimate is due. The directors have promised a generous one. I need the accrual to match the promise, not the rulebook. The rulebook says nothing has been earned yet.
scene.fin.tet_bonus_calc.c1: Calculate the accrual from the plan as it stands, and show Duc what the rulebook allows and what it does not.
scene.fin.tet_bonus_calc.c1.ok: Duc reads it. 'So, a smaller number, unless the directors formalise the promise.' He takes it to them, and a written plan follows.
scene.fin.tet_bonus_calc.c1.fail: The directors refuse to formalise it, and the accrual stays low. Staff grumble quietly about Finance.
scene.fin.tet_bonus_calc.c2: Accrue a moderate amount and note that the rest depends on a written decision by the directors.
scene.fin.tet_bonus_calc.c2.ok: Duc accepts the compromise. The note triggers a written decision in two weeks, and the year starts with a clean record.
scene.fin.tet_bonus_calc.c3: Accrue the full promised amount, as Duc asks.
scene.fin.tet_bonus_calc.c3.ok: Duc thanks you warmly. The books now show a liability nobody approved, and the profit looks lower than it should.
scene.fin.tet_bonus_calc.c3.fail: Hanh asks what approval supports the accrual. You point to Duc. Duc says he asked for 'an estimate'.
scene.fin.audit_notice_huddle.l1: The buyer's audit is in three weeks. They will look at revenue recognition, credit control and expenses. We have gaps in all three. Tell me where you would spend the time.
scene.fin.audit_notice_huddle.c1: List the gaps honestly with owners and dates, fix the worst first, and give Hanh the list so she can decide what to tell the buyer.
scene.fin.audit_notice_huddle.c1.ok: Hanh takes the list to Duc. The buyer is told honestly about two gaps with dated fixes. Audit readiness improves.
scene.fin.audit_notice_huddle.c2: Fix what can be fixed in three weeks and document the rest as known, without listing them for the buyer.
scene.fin.audit_notice_huddle.c2.ok: A pragmatic plan. Hanh accepts it, with a note that the gaps must be disclosed if asked.
scene.fin.audit_notice_huddle.c3: Concentrate on making the documents look complete and let the substance follow.
scene.fin.audit_notice_huddle.c3.ok: The files look good. The substance does not follow. You tell yourself there will be time after the audit.
scene.fin.audit_notice_huddle.c3.fail: Hanh notices a file that was created last week, dated three months ago. She does not ask. She simply looks at you.
scene.fin.dso_pressure.l1: The bank wants DSO below 55 days. We are at 63. Bao says the customers will pay, but not this quarter. I need you to think about what can reasonably be done with the receivables.
scene.fin.dso_pressure.c1: Propose real actions: earlier invoicing, a collections push on the five largest balances, and an honest forecast.
scene.fin.dso_pressure.c1.ok: DSO falls to 58 over the quarter: not enough for the bank, but real. Duc presents it with a plan. The bank extends the deadline.
scene.fin.dso_pressure.c1.fail: The collections push brings in less than hoped, and DSO stays at 61. You give Duc the facts. He says it is not what he wanted to hear.
scene.fin.dso_pressure.c2: Offer a small early-payment discount to a few customers, approved by Duc, to pull cash in.
scene.fin.dso_pressure.c2.ok: Three customers take it. Cash improves, margin falls slightly, and the approval is on file. A legitimate trade-off, openly made.
scene.fin.dso_pressure.c3: Reclassify the slowest balances as 'other receivables' so they fall out of the DSO calculation.
scene.fin.dso_pressure.c3.ok: DSO drops to 52. Duc says it is excellent work. The balances are still owed, and still late, and now harder to see.
scene.fin.dso_pressure.c3.fail: The auditor compares the DSO to the ageing report and the receivables note. The numbers do not reconcile.
scene.fin.year_end_close.l1: It is the last week of the year. I am 400 million short of the annual target, and I have two shipments that leave on the second of January. Book them this year. It is the same goods, just a few days.
scene.fin.year_end_close.l2: This will be audited. It is your call, and I will support what you decide. But decide knowing that.
scene.fin.year_end_close.c1: Refuse: they belong to next year, and say so clearly to Bao and to Duc in writing.
scene.fin.year_end_close.c1.ok: Bao is angry and the year ends below target. Hanh nods once. In January, the auditor's note says: 'Cut-off at year end was properly applied.'
scene.fin.year_end_close.c1.fail: Duc overrules you and asks someone else to book it. You have a written record, and not much else.
scene.fin.year_end_close.c2: Offer to book what has actually shipped by the 31st, and help Bao find more that can legitimately go out.
scene.fin.year_end_close.c2.ok: Bao finds one shipment that can leave on the 30th. It is not everything. It is honest, and he owes you one.
scene.fin.year_end_close.c3.ok: The year closes at target. Bao embraces you. The entries carry December dates and January dispatch logs.
scene.fin.year_end_close.c3.fail: The auditor's year-end cut-off test picks both shipments. The dispatch logs are dated the second of January. The error is material.
fact.skipped_cutoff_check: you skipped checking the cut-off before the auditor did
lesson.skipped_cutoff_check: Letting the auditor find your errors is a choice to be caught rather than to fix. A self-check costs an afternoon and changes how everything else is read.
scene.sales.tet_bonus_team.l1: The sales team's Tet bonus depends on what ships before the holiday. Everyone is counting on it, including you. Lan says her line cannot do it. I say she can, if she is told it matters. Can you make it matter to her?
scene.sales.tet_bonus_team.c1: Sit with Lan and build a shipping plan from what the line can really do, then tell the buyers the real dates.
scene.sales.tet_bonus_team.c1.ok: The plan ships sixty percent before Tet, on dates the buyers accept. The bonus is smaller. Lan brings you tea the next day without a word.
scene.sales.tet_bonus_team.c1.fail: One buyer will not accept the later date and cancels. The team bonus takes the hit, and the room remembers who brought the plan.
scene.sales.tet_bonus_team.c2: Ask Lan which orders are safest to rush, and promise only those.
scene.sales.tet_bonus_team.c2.ok: Lan picks three orders. They ship. The rest wait for January, honestly communicated. It is a workable, unheroic plan.
scene.sales.tet_bonus_team.c3: Promise the buyers their Tet dates, and tell Lan the dates are already fixed.
scene.sales.tet_bonus_team.c3.ok: Lan is furious and does it anyway. Most orders make the date. Two do not, and the buyer hears about it from you on the day.
scene.sales.tet_bonus_team.c3.fail: Half the orders miss the date, and Lan sends you the production log with your promises, and the times, in red.
arc.trade_fair_lead.title: The fair lead
scene.sales.fair_lead_sample.l1: I am forwarding a lead from the fair, a retailer in the Netherlands. They want a sample set in a finish we do not normally make: brushed, with a copper base. They need it in three weeks to show their board.
scene.sales.fair_lead_sample.c1: Ask production and QC whether it can be made, tell the retailer the real lead time, and offer a simpler sample in the meantime.
scene.sales.fair_lead_sample.c1.ok: Production needs five weeks for the copper base. The retailer accepts the simpler sample first and the copper one later. Nobody is surprised.
scene.sales.fair_lead_sample.c1.fail: The retailer says five weeks is too long and goes to a competitor. It is an honest loss, and a clean one.
scene.sales.fair_lead_sample.c2: Offer the copper base in three weeks with the current line, and check the detail with Lan after.
scene.sales.fair_lead_sample.c2.ok: The retailer is delighted. Lan finds a way, and gives you a look that says never do this again.
scene.sales.fair_lead_sample.c2.fail: The copper base cannot be done in three weeks. You tell the retailer on day nineteen. They are not pleased.
scene.sales.fair_lead_sample.c3: Promise the sample, and send a standard set dressed up as the finish they asked for.
scene.sales.fair_lead_sample.c3.ok: The sample arrives, looks close enough from a photo, and the board likes it. The retailer orders the real thing.
scene.sales.fair_lead_sample.c3.fail: The retailer's board member picks up the pot and taps the base. It rings hollow. The meeting ends quickly.
scene.sales.fair_lead_deal.l1: The Dutch retailer is ready to sign. Their contract has a late-delivery penalty of two percent per week, uncapped. Legal says it is aggressive. The volume is very good. What do we do?
scene.sales.fair_lead_deal.c1: Negotiate a cap and a grace period with the retailer, and tell Bao what you will not sign as written.
scene.sales.fair_lead_deal.c1.ok: A four-percent cap and a one-week grace are agreed. The retailer says: 'Most suppliers sign without reading.' You have a contract you can keep.
scene.sales.fair_lead_deal.c1.fail: The retailer will not move and walks away. Bao says it is a pity. Finance says it was the right call.
scene.sales.fair_lead_deal.c2: Sign with the penalty, but price it in and plan production with a buffer for the dates in the contract.
scene.sales.fair_lead_deal.c2.ok: It is a risk taken knowingly, priced and planned. Duc signs it off. Lan asks for a buffer and gets it.
scene.sales.fair_lead_deal.c3: Sign it as written, and promise Bao the delivery dates will be fine.
scene.sales.fair_lead_deal.c3.ok: The contract is signed. Bao is thrilled. You have promised something you do not control, with an uncapped penalty behind it.
scene.sales.fair_lead_deal.c3.fail: In the second month a shipment is delayed by nine days. The penalty is larger than the order's margin. Duc asks who signed.
scene.sales.finance_interview.l1: I have been comparing freight charges by customer. Mr Anders's account pays about half the average. There is no contract clause that explains it. Before I take this to Duc, I wanted to ask you what you know.
scene.sales.finance_interview.c1: Tell her the truth: the discounts were above your limit, you moved them into freight, and you can reconstruct every one.
scene.sales.finance_interview.c1.ok: Hanh is quiet, then says: 'Thank you for not making me find every line myself.' You get a formal warning, and the accounts are restated honestly.
scene.sales.finance_interview.c2: Say the freight rates were negotiated on a separate basis, and offer to find the paperwork.
scene.sales.finance_interview.c2.ok: Hanh waits a week for the paperwork, receives something plausible, and closes the query, for now.
scene.sales.finance_interview.c2.fail: The paperwork you produce is dated after the freight invoices. Hanh looks at the two dates, then at you.
scene.sales.finance_interview.c3: Say it was Bao's arrangement, and you only followed it.
scene.sales.finance_interview.c3.ok: Bao, called in, does not deny it, and takes a formal warning. You have made an enemy who holds a lot of your quota.
scene.sales.finance_interview.c3.fail: Bao produces your emails setting up the freight lines, in your own words. Hanh reads them while you watch.
scene.sales.quynh_promotion.l1: Quynh has been offered a coordinator role in the export team. Before I approve it, I asked if you would write me a reference. She speaks highly of you. Tell me honestly how she is doing.
scene.sales.quynh_promotion.c1: Write an honest reference: her strengths, the habits she picked up that need unlearning, and the support she will need.
scene.sales.quynh_promotion.c1.ok: Bao reads it twice. Quynh gets the role, with a mentor assigned. She reads the reference later, and writes you a note that just says: 'Thank you for telling the truth about me.'
scene.sales.quynh_promotion.c2: Write a warm, general reference that says she is promising.
scene.sales.quynh_promotion.c2.ok: Quynh gets the role. The reference says nothing that is false, and nothing that will help her with the difficult parts.
scene.sales.quynh_promotion.c3: Write a glowing reference that leaves out the shortcuts she learned from you.
scene.sales.quynh_promotion.c3.ok: Quynh is promoted, and starts teaching the new coordinators what she learned. Bao is pleased with his choice.
scene.sales.quynh_promotion.c3.fail: In her first month, Quynh quotes an impossible date to a buyer. The buyer quotes your reference back to Bao.
fact.misrepresented_sample: you sent a sample that was not what you told the customer it was
lesson.misrepresented_sample: A sample is a promise about the product. A sample dressed up as something it is not wins the order and loses the customer the first time they tap the base.
fact.accepted_unrealistic_terms: you signed contract terms you knew production could not meet
lesson.accepted_unrealistic_terms: Signing terms you cannot meet is a promise with a bill attached. The penalty clause is paid by the company, but the signature is yours.
fact.polished_reference: you wrote a reference that left out what a junior colleague most needed help with
lesson.polished_reference: A reference is a service to the next manager and to the person. Leaving out the difficult truth helps neither, and it keeps the habit alive.
role.prod.planner.title: Production Planner
role.prod.manager.title: Production Manager
role.prod.planner.blurb: You plan the lines of a cookware factory. Your pressures: dates that sales promised, overtime that gets stretched, maintenance that keeps being pushed back, and the guard someone asks you to leave off just for today.
char.kiet.name: Kiet
char.kiet.title: Line 2 supervisor
char.mai.name: Ms Mai
char.mai.title: Maintenance lead
char.phuc.name: Phuc
char.phuc.title: Press operator (new)
char.sang.name: Mr Sang
char.sang.title: Labour safety inspector
scene.prod.first_week.l1: Welcome to planning. The schedule for this week is on the board. Kiet runs line 2 and he will tell you what the board does not. Learn the lines before you learn the spreadsheet.
scene.prod.first_week.l2: With respect, most planners never walk the floor. Do not be one of them. Ask me how long a changeover really takes, not how long it says on the sheet.
scene.prod.first_week.c1: Spend the morning on line 2 with Kiet, timing the real changeover and noting where the sheet is wrong.
scene.prod.first_week.c1.ok: The sheet says 40 minutes. The real time is 75. Kiet sees you write it down, and says: 'Now you can plan.' The crew nods at you in the canteen afterwards.
scene.prod.first_week.c2: Take the standard times from the sheet and check them against two or three lines as you go.
scene.prod.first_week.c2.ok: It is a workable start. You find two wrong times by accident, in the second week, when a shift runs late.
scene.prod.first_week.c3: Trust the sheet. It was built by people who know the lines.
scene.prod.first_week.c3.ok: Your first plan looks perfect on paper. Kiet reads it, says nothing, and pins a corrected version beside it.
scene.prod.first_week.c3.fail: The plan puts 40 minutes on a changeover that takes 75. Line 2 runs an hour late every day for a week, and Lan asks whose numbers those were.
scene.prod.midyear_review.l1: Half a year. Your plans are more accurate than last year's planner's, and the crews trust them more. But I hear sales thinks you slow them down. How do you see that?
scene.prod.midyear_review.c1: Show her the on-time numbers, and the cases where an honest date saved a worse delay.
scene.prod.midyear_review.c1.ok: Lan goes through the cases. 'I will tell Bao to come to you before he promises a date. That is what you should be telling me.' You leave with a real rule.
scene.prod.midyear_review.c1.fail: Lan agrees with the numbers but says the company cannot win every argument with data. She asks you to be more commercial, and you are not sure what she means.
scene.prod.midyear_review.c2: Say you will try to give sales options, not just refusals, and ask her which orders matter most.
scene.prod.midyear_review.c2.ok: Lan brightens: 'Yes. A planner who brings options is worth two who bring walls.' She gives you her own priority list.
scene.prod.midyear_review.c3: Say sales asks for things that cannot be done, and the problem is theirs.
scene.prod.midyear_review.c3.ok: Lan sighs, partly agreeing. 'It is true, but it is not a plan.' She marks you down for defensiveness.
scene.prod.midyear_review.c3.fail: Bao has already spoken to Lan. She has his version, which has three examples of you saying no to a date you could have met.
scene.prod.big_breakdown_twist.l1: Line 1's forming press has stopped. A hydraulic seal has gone, and the spare is in another city. It is at least four days, more if the courier is slow. You have a rush order of eight thousand units due next Friday.
scene.prod.big_breakdown_twist.l2: Whatever it takes. Move it to another line, run the weekend, I do not care. The buyer has been promised.
scene.prod.big_breakdown_twist.c1: Re-plan honestly: which part can move to line 3, which part cannot, and tell Bao and the buyer the real date today.
scene.prod.big_breakdown_twist.c1.ok: Half moves to line 3 on two shifts. The other half slips three days. Bao hates it, the buyer accepts it, and the crews can do what you planned.
scene.prod.big_breakdown_twist.c1.fail: The buyer refuses the delay and cancels the second half. Bao says so in front of Lan. You have an honest plan and a smaller order.
scene.prod.big_breakdown_twist.c2: Move what can move to line 3 on a legal double shift, and ask Bao to split the delivery with the buyer.
scene.prod.big_breakdown_twist.c2.ok: It is a workable middle. The buyer takes two deliveries. The crews are tired but within limits, and Bao is merely unhappy.
scene.prod.big_breakdown_twist.c3: Tell Bao it will be fine, and work out the shifts afterwards, even if it means running the crews past what is allowed.
scene.prod.big_breakdown_twist.c3.ok: Bao is delighted. The crews run nights and a Sunday and most of the order makes the date. Nobody records the overtime.
scene.prod.big_breakdown_twist.c3.fail: On Saturday night a tired operator drops a die and nearly loses a hand. The line stops, and Kiet looks at the plan you posted.
scene.prod.sang_inspection.l1: I am here for the annual inspection. I would like to see the presses, the guards, the overtime records and the maintenance log for the last six months. I start on the floor, not in the office.
scene.prod.sang_inspection.l2: Show him what he asks for. Do not guess. If you do not know, say you will find out.
scene.prod.sang_inspection.c1: Walk him through the real floor and the real records, including the things you know are not ideal, and what you are doing about each.
scene.prod.sang_inspection.c1.ok: Sang spends two hours on line 2 and writes four observations. None is serious. 'Records that match the floor. I wish that were less unusual.' Kiet shakes your hand afterwards.
scene.prod.sang_inspection.c2: Tidy the obvious problems honestly, answer his questions, and produce the records he asks for.
scene.prod.sang_inspection.c2.ok: A routine inspection. Sang notes two items, both already on Mai's list. You come out with nothing to hide and no credit either.
scene.prod.sang_inspection.c3: Prepare a show: replace the guards that came off, clean the floor, and have the records look complete.
scene.prod.sang_inspection.c3.ok: Sang sees a perfect floor. He looks at the new paint on the guard brackets. He asks how long ago they were installed, and accepts the answer.
scene.prod.sang_inspection.c3.fail: A worker tells Sang, politely, that the guard on press 3 was put back this morning. Sang checks the maintenance log and the overtime sheet next.
scene.prod.year_end_review.l1: Annual review. Before I give you my view, tell me how you would rate your own year, and what you would plan differently.
scene.prod.year_end_review.c1: Give an honest account, including the plans that were too optimistic and the corners you saw being cut.
scene.prod.year_end_review.c1.ok: Lan is quiet for a long moment. She writes: 'Plans what can be done, not what is wanted.' It is the best thing you have read about yourself.
scene.prod.year_end_review.c2: Stay modest: list the wins and one thing to improve.
scene.prod.year_end_review.c2.ok: A safe review. Lan nods and moves to the next topic.
scene.prod.year_end_review.c3: Present the year as a success and leave out the nights and Sundays nobody recorded.
scene.prod.year_end_review.c3.ok: It lands well. You leave with a good rating and a small weight in your chest.
scene.prod.year_end_review.c3.fail: Lan has Kiet's shift records open on her desk. She turns them towards you without a word.
scene.prod.manager_offer.l1: I am moving to plant director at the end of the year. The directors asked me who should run production. I named you. One condition: every week, someone will ask you to bend a limit, just this once. I need to know what you will say.
scene.prod.manager_offer.c1: Accept, and say plainly which limits you will not bend, and that the directors must hear it from you first.
scene.prod.manager_offer.c1.ok: Lan smiles. 'Then it is yours. Write them on the wall of the planning office.' You take over the floor with the limits in writing.
scene.prod.manager_offer.c2: Thank her, but decline: you would rather plan than manage the pressure.
scene.prod.manager_offer.c2.ok: Lan looks disappointed, then understanding. 'The next manager may not be as careful as you.'
scene.prod.manager_offer.c3: Accept without asking what the condition means in practice.
scene.prod.manager_offer.c3.ok: Lan nods slowly and the directors congratulate you a little too warmly. You realise you agreed to something you did not ask about.
scene.prod.resignation_thought.l1: You look like you have not slept. With respect: I have seen planners go home at nine every night and leave by the summer. Are you all right?
scene.prod.resignation_thought.c1: Talk to Lan about the workload, and ask her to take a rush order off your plate.
scene.prod.resignation_thought.c1.ok: Lan listens, reassigns the changeover tracking to Kiet for two months, and says she should have noticed sooner.
scene.prod.resignation_thought.c1.fail: Lan nods and says everyone is stretched this quarter. You leave with sympathy and the same workload.
scene.prod.resignation_thought.c2: Hand in your resignation, politely, with a month's notice.
scene.prod.resignation_thought.c2.ok: Lan reads it twice and does not argue. You walk out of the gate lighter than you walked in.
scene.prod.resignation_thought.c3: Tell Kiet you are fine and keep going.
scene.prod.resignation_thought.c3.ok: Kiet nods and does not push. You feel slightly worse afterwards for having said it.
fact.exceeded_overtime_limit: you ran crews beyond the overtime limit and did not record it
lesson.exceeded_overtime_limit: An overtime limit exists because tired people make mistakes with machines. Running past it, and leaving it off the record, hides the risk from everyone who could have stopped it.
fact.staged_safety_inspection: you staged the floor for a safety inspection
lesson.staged_safety_inspection: An inspection tests how the floor really is. A staged floor tells the inspector nothing and tells the workers that safety is for show.
arc.the_promise.title: The promise
scene.prod.impossible_date.l1: I have promised Mr Anders fifteen thousand units in three weeks. I know, I know. The buyer needs them for a promotion and I could not say no. Tell me it is possible.
scene.prod.impossible_date.l2: It is your plan. I will back what is honest. Tell us what the lines can really do.
scene.prod.impossible_date.c1: Show the real capacity: eleven thousand in three weeks without breaking any limit, fifteen in five. Offer a split delivery.
scene.prod.impossible_date.c1.ok: Bao groans and calls Anders. Anders accepts two deliveries. You have a plan that is possible, and a salesman who owes you an apology.
scene.prod.impossible_date.c1.fail: Anders will not split the order and gives the second half to a rival. You are right, and poorer for it.
scene.prod.impossible_date.c2: Offer thirteen thousand by adding a legal third shift on line 3, and ask Bao to negotiate the last two thousand.
scene.prod.impossible_date.c2.ok: It is a stretch within limits. Kiet agrees to try it for two weeks. Bao negotiates a one-week extension on the rest.
scene.prod.impossible_date.c3: Say it is possible, and work out how afterwards.
scene.prod.impossible_date.c3.ok: Bao kisses the air. The plan on your desk needs eighteen percent more capacity than exists. You add optimistic times and close the spreadsheet.
scene.prod.impossible_date.c3.fail: Kiet reads the plan on the board and laughs, not happily. He takes it to Lan before lunch.
scene.prod.extra_shifts.l1: We are four days behind and my crew has worked twelve days straight. With respect, I need to know: are we going to be asked to work Sunday again, and will it be written down?
scene.prod.extra_shifts.c1: Stay within the limit: rotate crews, bring in two temps for the weekend, and record every hour.
scene.prod.extra_shifts.c1.ok: The temps slow the line at first, but it holds. Kiet's crew gets its Sunday back. You ship a day late and everyone knows why.
scene.prod.extra_shifts.c1.fail: The temps are not trained for the press, so you keep them off it. The weekend is thin. Bao shouts, and Kiet stays quiet.
scene.prod.extra_shifts.c2: Ask the crew to volunteer for Sunday, pay the premium, and record it, knowing it is close to the limit.
scene.prod.extra_shifts.c2.ok: Nine of twelve volunteer. You record all the hours, and Lan signs the approval. It is a judgement call, made in the open.
scene.prod.extra_shifts.c3: Run them Sunday and Monday night too, and leave the extra hours off the sheet.
scene.prod.extra_shifts.c3.ok: The order catches up. The sheet shows a normal week. Kiet does not thank you, and does not say no.
scene.prod.extra_shifts.c3.fail: A worker faints at the press on Monday night. The first-aider asks how many hours he has worked. The sheet says forty-four.
scene.prod.guard_off_today.l1: The guard on press 3 slows the operators by about twelve percent, because they have to reach around it. I would never say this, but I have been asked to. Can the guard come off for today only? It will get us back on schedule.
scene.prod.guard_off_today.c1: Refuse: the guard stays on. Find the twelve percent elsewhere: a changeover saved, a batch moved, or a later date.
scene.prod.guard_off_today.c1.ok: You find nine of the twelve. The rest becomes a one-day delay that Bao will complain about. Kiet says, quietly: 'Thank you.'
scene.prod.guard_off_today.c1.fail: There is nothing left to find. The order slips two days, and you hold the line in a room that does not like it.
scene.prod.guard_off_today.c2: Slow the line to a safer rhythm with a second operator on the feed, and re-plan the loss.
scene.prod.guard_off_today.c2.ok: The press runs slower but safe. You recover part of the loss on line 4. Kiet nods, with some doubt about how long it will last.
scene.prod.guard_off_today.c3: Tell him to take it off for today, and put it back tomorrow.
scene.prod.guard_off_today.c3.ok: The guard comes off. The press runs faster. The catch-up works. Nobody puts the guard back on Tuesday, and you do not ask.
scene.prod.guard_off_today.c3.fail: Phuc's sleeve is caught by the press on the first morning. He pulls free, unhurt, white as paper. The guard sits on the floor by the wall.
scene.prod.near_miss.l1: There was a near miss at press 3 this morning. Nobody is hurt. Phuc is in the canteen, shaking. The rule is that near misses are reported to Lan and logged. You decide what goes in the log.
scene.prod.near_miss.c1: Stop the press, report it in full to Lan and log it with the cause, including what you asked for that week.
scene.prod.near_miss.c1.ok: Lan is silent for a long time. 'Thank you for telling me all of it.' The schedule is re-planned, the guard goes back, and you are given a formal warning for the decision that led here.
scene.prod.near_miss.c2: Log the near miss and put the guard back, but describe the cause as operator error.
scene.prod.near_miss.c2.ok: The log says what it says. The guard is back. Phuc reads the log and looks at you once, then nods as if he expected it.
scene.prod.near_miss.c2.fail: Kiet, asked by Lan, says plainly that the guard was off on your instruction. The log and his account are side by side.
scene.prod.near_miss.c3: Do not log it, put the guard back quietly, and ask everyone to forget it.
scene.prod.near_miss.c3.ok: Nobody says anything. The near miss exists only in people's heads. Phuc has started wearing a glove on the other hand.
scene.prod.near_miss.c3.fail: A week later the inspector's questionnaire asks the crew whether any near misses were left off the log. Four people tick yes.
arc.deferred_maintenance.title: The deferred maintenance
scene.prod.maintenance_request.l1: The annealing oven on line 1 is overdue for its service by three weeks. I have put in the request twice. The thermocouple is drifting, and I am worried. I need two days of downtime. Write it into the plan, please.
scene.prod.maintenance_request.c1: Schedule the two days now, in the quietest week you can find, and tell Lan and Bao what it costs.
scene.prod.maintenance_request.c1.ok: It costs a day of output. Bao complains. Mai services the oven properly and finds the thermocouple was off by eleven degrees. She writes it in the log, and gives you a copy.
scene.prod.maintenance_request.c1.fail: The chosen week turns out to be the week a rush order arrives. You hold the shutdown, and Bao never forgives the timing.
scene.prod.maintenance_request.c2: Split it: one day now and one day in the holiday week, and agree the split with Mai in writing.
scene.prod.maintenance_request.c2.ok: Mai accepts, not happily. 'Half is better than nothing, as long as the second day happens.' It goes into the plan with a date.
scene.prod.maintenance_request.c3: Tell her it will go in after the peak, and make a note to do it later.
scene.prod.maintenance_request.c3.ok: Mai does not argue. She writes the date in her logbook, your name next to it, and the word 'deferred'.
scene.prod.maintenance_defer.l1: The peak is starting. I know Mai has a service booked on line 1. I need that oven running every day for the next six weeks. Can it wait until the peak is over? I will take responsibility.
scene.prod.maintenance_defer.c1: Hold to the date: bring Mai's findings and what the drifting thermocouple can do to the product and the crew.
scene.prod.maintenance_defer.c1.ok: Lan reads Mai's note twice. 'Then do it on Saturday and Sunday. We will take the loss.' She signs it herself.
scene.prod.maintenance_defer.c1.fail: Lan says the peak cannot be touched, and asks you to write the deferral down with her name on it. Mai is listening at the door.
scene.prod.maintenance_defer.c2: Agree a hard date after the peak, written down and signed, with a spare thermocouple on standby in the meantime.
scene.prod.maintenance_defer.c2.ok: It is a real compromise with a real date and a real spare. Mai agrees, because the risk is now named and owned.
scene.prod.maintenance_defer.c3: Defer it past the peak without a date, and tell Mai it will be soon.
scene.prod.maintenance_defer.c3.ok: The oven runs through the peak. The shutdown disappears from the plan. Mai's logbook gets a new line, and she stops asking.
scene.prod.maintenance_defer.c3.fail: The thermocouple drifts further. A batch comes out under-annealed and is scrapped. Mai shows you her logbook, without comment.
scene.prod.breakdown.l1: The annealing oven on line 1 has failed in the middle of the peak. Three days to repair, at best. The logbook shows it was due for service eleven weeks ago, and what was said about it.
scene.prod.breakdown.l2: I need to know, for the directors, how this happened. Tell me what I should say.
scene.prod.breakdown.c1: Give Lan the whole sequence: Mai's requests, the deferrals, and your part in them, and propose a recovery plan.
scene.prod.breakdown.c1.ok: Lan listens and writes it down. To the directors she says: 'We deferred it, we knew the risk, and here is the fix.' It is an uncomfortable meeting, and you keep your credibility.
scene.prod.breakdown.c2: Say the decision was made jointly, by planning, production and maintenance, in the peak.
scene.prod.breakdown.c2.ok: It is roughly true and shares the damage around. Mai reads the minutes and is silent. The directors accept it and ask for a process change.
scene.prod.breakdown.c3: Say maintenance never flagged it as urgent, and suggest that the maintenance log is unreliable.
scene.prod.breakdown.c3.ok: The directors turn on maintenance. Mai is placed under review. She looks at you across the canteen and says nothing.
scene.prod.breakdown.c3.fail: Mai produces her logbook: each request, each date, each reply, including yours. The logbook is stamped by the safety officer every month.
arc.phuc.title: Phuc
scene.prod.phuc_training.l1: I am supposed to run the press by myself from next week. I have only watched it for three days. I do not like to ask, but can I have a proper training session? I want to do it right.
scene.prod.phuc_training.c1: Schedule a full training with Kiet and the safety sheet, and do not put Phuc on the press alone until he is signed off.
scene.prod.phuc_training.c1.ok: Two days of training, and a sign-off sheet. Phuc is proud of his card. Kiet adds a line to his own notebook: 'Planner keeps to sign-off.'
scene.prod.phuc_training.c2: Pair him with an experienced operator for two weeks and check in on him.
scene.prod.phuc_training.c2.ok: It helps. Phuc learns the rhythm of the press. There is no sign-off sheet, but there is a person who will speak up if something is wrong.
scene.prod.phuc_training.c3: Tell him he will pick it up as he goes, the press is simple.
scene.prod.phuc_training.c3.ok: Phuc nods. He does not ask again. He will learn it, one way or another, on the job.
scene.prod.phuc_unsupervised.l1: We are two short on line 2 this week, with one sick and one at a funeral. The only way the plan works is if Phuc runs the press alone on the night shift. He has done it twice with someone nearby. With respect: should he?
scene.prod.phuc_unsupervised.c1: No: keep Phuc on supervised work, re-plan the night shift around what the crew can safely do, and tell Bao the date slips.
scene.prod.phuc_unsupervised.c1.ok: The night shift runs at seventy percent. Bao shouts. Kiet says nothing, but the next morning he brings you a coffee.
scene.prod.phuc_unsupervised.c1.fail: No replacement can be found and the night shift is cancelled. You lose a day, and Bao makes sure Lan knows it was your choice.
scene.prod.phuc_unsupervised.c2: Put Phuc on the press with Kiet checking on him every half hour, and log it as supervised work.
scene.prod.phuc_unsupervised.c2.ok: It is thin, but Kiet can do it. The night shift runs. Phuc is nervous, and careful. Nothing goes wrong, and you do not relax.
scene.prod.phuc_unsupervised.c3: Yes: put Phuc on the press alone, it is only one night.
scene.prod.phuc_unsupervised.c3.ok: The night shift runs at full speed. Phuc is exhausted and proud. You do not ask how it went.
scene.prod.phuc_unsupervised.c3.fail: At 2 a.m. the press cycles with Phuc's hand too close. He pulls back, but the tip of a finger is caught. The night supervisor calls you at home.
scene.prod.phuc_incident.l1: Phuc has hurt his hand on the press. It is not serious, but it is reportable. The report goes to the safety office and the insurer. You wrote the night plan. I need you to write the account, and I will sign it.
scene.prod.phuc_incident.c1: Write the account as it was: the plan, the short staffing, who was supervising and what you asked for.
scene.prod.phuc_incident.c1.ok: Lan reads it twice and signs it without changing a word. Phuc is paid in full during recovery, and the night plan rule is rewritten. You get a formal warning, and keep Kiet's trust.
scene.prod.phuc_incident.c2: Write a short, factual account that leaves out who decided the night staffing.
scene.prod.phuc_incident.c2.ok: Lan signs it. The account is accurate and incomplete. The insurer asks no questions. Phuc reads it and says only that it is fine.
scene.prod.phuc_incident.c3: Write that Phuc operated the press without authorisation, against instructions.
scene.prod.phuc_incident.c3.ok: Lan signs it without looking closely. Phuc is placed on a formal warning, loses the night premium and does not look at you again.
scene.prod.phuc_incident.c3.fail: Kiet hands Lan the night plan with your initials on it, and the shift roster showing Phuc was assigned. The report and the documents disagree.
arc.materials.title: The late steel
scene.prod.material_late.l1: I have bad news about the steel for next week. The supplier is three days late. It is not my fault, it is the port. You will have to shuffle the schedule, and I would rather you did not mention it to Bao.
scene.prod.material_late.c1: Re-plan openly: move orders around the gap, tell Lan and Bao the new dates, and log the reason.
scene.prod.material_late.c1.ok: Two orders move, and one is delayed by two days. Bao is irritated. Tam is embarrassed. The plan works, and everyone can see why it changed.
scene.prod.material_late.c1.fail: The steel is five days late, not three. You re-plan twice. Bao says 'I thought planning could handle this.'
scene.prod.material_late.c2: Run the orders that can run with what is on hand, and tell sales only that one order will be late.
scene.prod.material_late.c2.ok: It is accurate: one order is late. The fuller story, about the steel, is still in your notes. Tam thanks you quietly.
scene.prod.material_late.c3: Tell nobody. Re-plan quietly and hope the steel arrives in time.
scene.prod.material_late.c3.ok: The steel arrives on the fourth day. You lose a day of output and nobody notices. Tam owes you one.
scene.prod.material_late.c3.fail: The steel is late by a week. By the time you say so, sales has promised the delivery to the buyer twice.
scene.prod.stockout_cover.l1: Mr Anders wants to know whether his order will ship on the date I gave him. The lines say it cannot because of the steel, and I am hearing it for the first time in a corridor. Tell me it is fine.
scene.prod.stockout_cover.c1: Tell him the truth, with a plan: the real new date, and what you can do to shorten it.
scene.prod.stockout_cover.c1.ok: Bao swears, then calls Anders. Anders says: 'Better to hear it now.' The new date holds. Bao thanks you, in his own way, three weeks later.
scene.prod.stockout_cover.c2: Say there is a risk, and that you will confirm by Friday after you check with Tam.
scene.prod.stockout_cover.c2.ok: Bao accepts, anxiously. The truth arrives on Friday and is no better. But no one can say you hid it.
scene.prod.stockout_cover.c3: Say it is fine. Sort out the steel afterwards.
scene.prod.stockout_cover.c3.ok: Bao relays it to Anders. The steel arrives a day before the date, and you manage to squeeze the order in. You were lucky.
scene.prod.stockout_cover.c3.fail: The steel does not arrive. The order ships a week late. Anders asks Bao who told him it was fine. Bao tells him.
fact.planned_unrealistic_shifts: you planned shifts that the lines and the crews could not deliver
lesson.planned_unrealistic_shifts: A plan that needs more capacity than exists is a promise in a spreadsheet. It becomes overtime, skipped steps or shortcuts, and the planner wrote it.
fact.bypassed_guard: you had a safety guard taken off a machine to run faster
lesson.bypassed_guard: A guard is the difference between a near miss and an injury. Taking it off to catch up saves a day and moves the risk onto the operator's hands.
fact.stopped_the_line: you kept a safety guard on and found the time somewhere else
lesson.stopped_the_line: Refusing to trade safety for speed costs a day and earns the trust of the people whose hands are at risk. It is also what a fair inspection looks for.
fact.reported_near_miss: you reported a near miss in full, including your own part
lesson.reported_near_miss: Near-miss reports are how the next injury is prevented. Reporting your own part in one is what makes people believe the rest of your reports.
fact.hid_near_miss: you left a near miss off the log
lesson.hid_near_miss: A near miss that is not logged teaches nobody anything. The same machine, the same shift and the same pressure will produce the next one.
fact.blamed_operator: you described an accident your plan caused as the operator's error
lesson.blamed_operator: Blaming the operator is the easiest move in the room and the most damaging. He has no power to correct the record, and he remembers.
fact.edited_incident_report: you wrote an incident report that left out who decided the staffing
lesson.edited_incident_report: An incident report is for the safety office, the insurer and the next shift. One that hides the decision protects the writer and deceives all three.
fact.accurate_incident_report: you wrote an incident report that included your own decision
lesson.accurate_incident_report: An accurate report costs a warning and keeps you credible. The next report you write will be believed.
fact.assigned_untrained_operator: you put an operator on a dangerous machine before he was trained
lesson.assigned_untrained_operator: Training is not a formality. Assigning someone to a press before they are signed off moves the risk from the plan to their hands.
fact.deferred_maintenance: you deferred maintenance that the maintenance lead had asked for
lesson.deferred_maintenance: Deferred maintenance is borrowed time. The interest is paid when the machine fails, usually at the worst moment and often on someone else's shift.
fact.owned_deferral: you told the truth about a deferral that led to a breakdown
lesson.owned_deferral: Saying what was deferred, and who decided, lets the company fix the process. Hiding it means the next breakdown comes from the same place.
fact.blamed_maintenance: you blamed the maintenance team for a failure you helped cause
lesson.blamed_maintenance: Maintenance keeps records because they expect to be blamed. Pointing at a logbook that contradicts you only makes the contradiction public.
fact.hid_stockout: you told sales a shipment was fine when you knew the material was missing
lesson.hid_stockout: A stock-out that is hidden from sales becomes a broken promise to a buyer. The earlier the truth is told, the more options the company has.
fact.ran_short_handed: you ran the lines short-handed and pushed the gap onto the crews
lesson.ran_short_handed: A crew that is asked to cover a gap covers it with tiredness. Running short-handed at full speed is overtime that is not counted.
fact.ignored_heat_risk: you kept crews working through dangerous heat without changing the plan
lesson.ignored_heat_risk: Heat is a safety condition, not a mood. A plan that ignores it pushes the risk onto whoever is weakest that afternoon.
fact.skipped_changeover_check: you skipped the first-article check after a changeover to save an hour
lesson.skipped_changeover_check: The first-article check is cheap insurance against a whole batch going wrong. Skipping it saves an hour and risks the day.
fact.pressured_qc_release: you leaned on quality control to release a lot it had held
lesson.pressured_qc_release: A hold is the quality manager's job. Pressuring someone to release it moves the risk from the lot to the person who signs.
fact.edited_overtime_log: you edited the gate log so it agreed with the overtime sheet
lesson.edited_overtime_log: Changing a record so two documents agree is falsification, however tidy it looks. The second copy, in the security company's files, rarely agrees.
fact.dismissed_worker_question: you dismissed a fair question from the crew about their pay
lesson.dismissed_worker_question: A question about pay is a question about fairness. Refusing to answer turns a question into a grievance.
fact.used_unapproved_subcontractor: you used an unapproved subcontractor and labelled the goods as made in-house
lesson.used_unapproved_subcontractor: An approved supplier list exists so that every pot can be traced. A subcontractor outside it, with a false label, breaks the trace and the trust.
fact.denied_emergency_leave: you refused a worker leave for a family emergency
lesson.denied_emergency_leave: An order will be shipped eventually. A refused emergency is remembered by a whole crew for years.
fact.blamed_boss: you told the directors your manager was responsible for a decision you made
lesson.blamed_boss: Signing is not the same as deciding. Pointing at your boss's signature when you made the decision turns her support into your exposure.
scene.prod.pre_tet_crunch.l1: Before Tet every buyer wants everything shipped. I have seven orders promised for the last week before the holiday, twice the normal volume. I told them yes. You have the plan, so just make it work.
scene.prod.pre_tet_crunch.c1: Build the honest plan: what ships before Tet, what ships after, and ask Bao to tell the buyers now.
scene.prod.pre_tet_crunch.c1.ok: Four of the seven ship before Tet. Bao tells the buyers early. Two accept January. One grumbles, and stays.
scene.prod.pre_tet_crunch.c1.fail: Two buyers will not wait for January and cancel. Bao is furious, and Lan is quiet. The crews have a calm last week.
scene.prod.pre_tet_crunch.c2: Prioritise by margin and buyer importance, squeeze a third shift inside the limit, and let Bao argue the rest.
scene.prod.pre_tet_crunch.c2.ok: Five of seven ship. Everyone is tired, nobody breaks a rule, and Kiet gives the crews the Saturday off after.
scene.prod.pre_tet_crunch.c3: Promise all seven, and work out how later.
scene.prod.pre_tet_crunch.c3.ok: Bao hugs you. The crews run six days a week for three weeks. Six orders ship, one does not, and the sheet shows forty-hour weeks.
scene.prod.pre_tet_crunch.c3.fail: In the last week two operators make costly errors from fatigue, and a pallet of pots is scrapped. The overtime sheet is checked by Lan.
scene.prod.tet_restart.l1: Two weeks after Tet and a third of the crew has not come back. Some are still in their home provinces, a few have found other jobs. The orders have not gone away. With respect, what is the plan?
scene.prod.tet_restart.c1: Re-plan for the crew you actually have, ask HR for proper temps with training, and tell sales what is realistic.
scene.prod.tet_restart.c1.ok: The first two weeks run at seventy percent. By week four the temps are trained and the lines recover. Kiet says it is the first time a planner asked him what the crew could do.
scene.prod.tet_restart.c1.fail: HR is slow and two of the temps leave in week three. You re-plan again, and Kiet does not reproach you, which helps a little.
scene.prod.tet_restart.c2: Run short-handed at the normal speed for a month, and ask the crews to cover.
scene.prod.tet_restart.c2.ok: The crews cover, grumbling. Output holds. By the end of the month three more have left. Kiet does not say 'I told you so'.
scene.prod.tet_restart.c2.fail: A tired operator makes a mistake on line 2 in week three. The crew blames the plan. The plan is yours.
scene.prod.tet_restart.c3: Ask the remaining crews to work longer shifts to cover the gap, without formal overtime.
scene.prod.tet_restart.c3.ok: They agree, because Tet bonuses were good. The gap closes. Nobody asks whether it is legal, and nobody writes it down.
scene.prod.tet_restart.c3.fail: One operator asks a neighbour at another factory what the law says. By Friday, three people are asking about their overtime pay.
scene.prod.heat_fatigue.l1: It is thirty-eight degrees on the floor by two in the afternoon. Mistakes are up. Two people have been dizzy. With respect, the shift plan was written for a cooler season. What do we change?
scene.prod.heat_fatigue.c1: Move the hardest work to early morning and evening, add water breaks, and accept the lower output.
scene.prod.heat_fatigue.c1.ok: Output falls eight percent and errors fall faster. Kiet moves the line fans himself. Lan says: 'Good call.'
scene.prod.heat_fatigue.c1.fail: The new shifts clash with transport for half the crew. Attendance drops, and the plan needs another round.
scene.prod.heat_fatigue.c2: Add ten-minute breaks and two fans, and keep the hours as they are.
scene.prod.heat_fatigue.c2.ok: It helps a little. Kiet says it is better than nothing. Nobody collapses this week.
scene.prod.heat_fatigue.c3: Push on: the crews have worked in heat before, and the orders will not wait.
scene.prod.heat_fatigue.c3.ok: The week passes. Two more people go home sick. Output holds. Kiet does not speak to you on Friday.
scene.prod.heat_fatigue.c3.fail: A worker collapses at the press on Thursday afternoon. The ambulance is called. The shift log shows no breaks that day.
scene.prod.changeover_shortcut.l1: Changeover on line 2 takes seventy-five minutes because of the die check and the first-article test. We are an hour behind. I have been asked, by someone I will not name, whether we can skip the first-article test just this once.
scene.prod.changeover_shortcut.c1: Keep the first-article test, and move something else to recover the hour.
scene.prod.changeover_shortcut.c1.ok: The test finds a die offset of half a millimetre. Kiet fixes it in ten minutes. Without the test, the whole batch would have been scrap.
scene.prod.changeover_shortcut.c1.fail: The test passes, and the hour is lost for nothing, or so it seems. Bao complains about the delay and does not hear the point.
scene.prod.changeover_shortcut.c2: Do the test on the first three pieces only, log the reduced check, and tell QC.
scene.prod.changeover_shortcut.c2.ok: Khoa reads the note and approves a reduced check for this run. It is a documented, approved compromise, and Kiet relaxes.
scene.prod.changeover_shortcut.c3: Skip it. The die was fine yesterday.
scene.prod.changeover_shortcut.c3.ok: The line starts on time and the batch is fine. Nobody notices that there is no first-article record.
scene.prod.changeover_shortcut.c3.fail: The die has shifted. Six hundred pots are scrapped before anyone notices, and QC asks for the first-article record.
scene.prod.qc_hold_conflict.l1: I have put a hold on the lot from line 3. The reading is on the edge and I want it retested. It will take a day. I know you need it for Friday.
scene.prod.qc_hold_conflict.l2: It is fine. QC is being overcautious again. Release it, and let us ship.
scene.prod.qc_hold_conflict.c1: Support the hold: replan Friday around a day's delay, and tell Bao what the retest is for.
scene.prod.qc_hold_conflict.c1.ok: The retest passes on Thursday. Friday is tight and meets the date. Khoa thanks you, which he rarely does. Bao shrugs.
scene.prod.qc_hold_conflict.c1.fail: The retest fails. The lot is scrapped and Friday is lost. You were right to hold it, and Bao never lets you forget it.
scene.prod.qc_hold_conflict.c2: Ask Khoa whether a partial retest on a sample can be done this afternoon, and plan around that.
scene.prod.qc_hold_conflict.c2.ok: Khoa agrees to a sample retest by four. It passes, and the lot releases. Everyone gets a little of what they wanted.
scene.prod.qc_hold_conflict.c3: Side with Bao and lean on Khoa to release it.
scene.prod.qc_hold_conflict.c3.ok: Khoa releases it with a note: 'Released under production pressure.' The date is met. The note is in the file.
scene.prod.qc_hold_conflict.c3.fail: Khoa refuses, and goes to Lan. Lan asks why the planner was leaning on the quality manager.
scene.prod.overtime_log.l1: The overtime sheet for last month does not match the gate logs. The gate log shows my crew worked 61 hours more than the sheet. The auditors look at the two side by side. Tell me how you want it handled.
scene.prod.overtime_log.c1: Correct the sheet to match the gate log, pay the crew for every hour, and tell Lan.
scene.prod.overtime_log.c1.ok: Payroll is surprised, then pays. The crew hears about it within an hour and the canteen is warmer towards you the next day.
scene.prod.overtime_log.c1.fail: Lan is unhappy about the cost and says so. She also says she would rather know than not. You are not sure that is a comfort.
scene.prod.overtime_log.c2: Explain the gap as breaks and clock-in delays, and adjust half the difference.
scene.prod.overtime_log.c2.ok: It is a partial fix. The crew is paid for half the hours, and you know the other half will come back.
scene.prod.overtime_log.c3: Edit the gate log entries so the two records agree.
scene.prod.overtime_log.c3.ok: The records agree. The crew is paid for the hours on the sheet and nobody questions it. Kiet looks at you for a long time.
scene.prod.overtime_log.c3.fail: The security company keeps its own copy of the gate logs. The two versions are compared in the inspector's file.
scene.prod.union_question.l1: A few of the crew asked me about overtime pay rates. They heard a neighbour's factory pays more on Sundays. They want to know what we pay and why. It is a fair question. Will you answer it, or should I?
scene.prod.union_question.c1: Get the actual rates from HR, explain them plainly to the crew, and say what you do not know.
scene.prod.union_question.c1.ok: You read the rates out in the canteen. One is lower than the crew expected, and you say so. The answers are accepted. Nobody complains, and several thank you.
scene.prod.union_question.c2: Tell them to ask HR, and offer to take the question to HR yourself.
scene.prod.union_question.c2.ok: It is correct and a little slow. HR replies in a week. The crew waits, and the question stays on the table.
scene.prod.union_question.c3: Tell them it is not their concern, and that rates are fixed by the company.
scene.prod.union_question.c3.ok: The questions stop. The mood on line 2 does not improve. Kiet says nothing and looks at the floor.
scene.prod.union_question.c3.fail: Two workers write to the labour office. The inspector's first question on the next visit is about overtime pay.
scene.prod.subcontractor_offer.l1: A small workshop across town has offered to make two thousand of the basic pots for us at a good price, this week. They are not on our approved list. They have done work for a competitor. It would save a lot of pressure on line 4.
scene.prod.subcontractor_offer.c1: Decline the workshop for now, propose a qualification audit, and plan line 4 honestly meanwhile.
scene.prod.subcontractor_offer.c1.ok: The audit takes three weeks and finds the workshop is decent but has no traceability. Khoa adds it to the approved list with conditions.
scene.prod.subcontractor_offer.c1.fail: The workshop finds other work in the meantime. Bao is annoyed. The pressure on line 4 is unchanged.
scene.prod.subcontractor_offer.c2: Use the workshop for one batch, with QC inspecting every incoming lot, and log it as a trial.
scene.prod.subcontractor_offer.c2.ok: The batch is acceptable. Khoa gets extra work and says so. The trial is documented, and Bao gets his relief.
scene.prod.subcontractor_offer.c3: Use them without telling QC, and mark the pots as made in-house.
scene.prod.subcontractor_offer.c3.ok: Two thousand pots ship on time. Line 4 breathes. The labels say what they should not.
scene.prod.subcontractor_offer.c3.fail: The buyer's auditor finds pots without the factory's weld marks in a shipment. Khoa is asked where they came from.
scene.prod.family_emergency.l1: One of my best operators got a call from home this morning: his father is in hospital, two hundred kilometres away. He wants to leave now. The shift is already short, and the order is due tomorrow.
scene.prod.family_emergency.c1: Let him go now, re-plan the shift around the gap, and tell Lan the order may slip.
scene.prod.family_emergency.c1.ok: The order ships six hours late. The operator's father recovers. The crew remembers that the planner let him go.
scene.prod.family_emergency.c1.fail: The order is a day late and the buyer complains. Lan says nothing about it, which is itself a kind of answer.
scene.prod.family_emergency.c2: Let him go at the end of his shift, and arrange a driver for him so he is not alone on the road.
scene.prod.family_emergency.c2.ok: It is a fair compromise. The operator arrives at midnight and his family is grateful. The order ships on time.
scene.prod.family_emergency.c3: Tell him the order comes first, and that he can go on Friday.
scene.prod.family_emergency.c3.ok: He stays, silent, and works the shift. The order ships on time. He does not look at you again.
