scene.prod.family_emergency.c3.fail: He leaves anyway at noon. The shift is thinner, and the crew talks about it on the canteen wall.
scene.prod.year_end_peak.l1: Year-end. The directors want the annual output record broken. Every line, every shift, for six weeks. I will back what you plan, but I want you to tell me honestly what is possible.
scene.prod.year_end_peak.c1: Plan the real maximum within the limits, with rotation and rest days, and show Lan what it yields.
scene.prod.year_end_peak.c1.ok: It is eight percent under the target and a new record anyway. Lan takes it to the directors: 'This is what we can do without breaking anyone.' They accept.
scene.prod.year_end_peak.c1.fail: The directors want the full target. Lan holds your plan up against the pressure, and it costs her some standing.
scene.prod.year_end_peak.c2: Stretch: use every legal hour and ask the crews to volunteer for more, and record it all.
scene.prod.year_end_peak.c2.ok: Nearly the target. The crews are exhausted but paid fairly, and the record is clean. You are proud of it, and worried for January.
scene.prod.year_end_peak.c3: Commit to the full target and work out the hours later, however many it takes.
scene.prod.year_end_peak.c3.ok: The target is hit on the last day of the year. The directors toast. The sheet shows a normal week. Kiet does not come to the toast.
scene.prod.year_end_peak.c3.fail: In week five a fatigued operator loses two fingers to a die. The ambulance takes him. The overtime sheet and the gate log tell two stories.
scene.prod.sang_asks_records.l1: I have interviewed the crew on press 3. Three of them independently said the guard was taken off for a week in the summer. I would like to see the planning records for that week, and hear from the planner what happened.
scene.prod.sang_asks_records.c1: Tell him what happened: who asked, what you agreed, and what you should have done. Give him the records.
scene.prod.sang_asks_records.c1.ok: Sang writes it all down. The finding is serious, but it is recorded as 'self-reported and corrected'. The guard procedure is rewritten, and you are given a formal warning.
scene.prod.sang_asks_records.c2: Give him the planning records, and say the guard removal was a supervisor's decision on the floor.
scene.prod.sang_asks_records.c2.ok: Sang looks at the records and notes that the plan for that week required the speed the guard prevented. He writes it down, carefully.
scene.prod.sang_asks_records.c2.fail: Kiet is called in and says, quietly, that he asked for the guard to stay on and was told no. He has a message on his phone.
scene.prod.sang_asks_records.c3: Say you do not recall the details, and offer to look.
scene.prod.sang_asks_records.c3.ok: Sang gives you a week. You find the plan and hand it over. It is not the whole truth, but it is something.
scene.prod.sang_asks_records.c3.fail: The crew gives Sang the shift records, which show the plan's original numbers and your name. He has them on the table next to your notes.
scene.prod.scapegoat_meeting.l1: The inspection report names the near-miss on press 3 and an incident report that does not match the shift records. The directors want to know who is responsible. They will decide tomorrow. I want to hear it from you first.
scene.prod.scapegoat_meeting.c1: Tell her the real account, including the operator's part, which was none, and your own.
scene.prod.scapegoat_meeting.c1.ok: Lan listens, and takes your account to the directors with her own signature beside it. You are demoted to assistant planner, and you keep your job and, eventually, your name.
scene.prod.scapegoat_meeting.c2: Say the operator was also responsible for not refusing an unsafe instruction.
scene.prod.scapegoat_meeting.c2.ok: The directors treat it as shared fault. Phuc is moved to another line, and everyone knows why.
scene.prod.scapegoat_meeting.c2.fail: Phuc has kept his own notes, and Kiet confirms them. The 'shared fault' argument does not survive the room.
scene.prod.scapegoat_meeting.c3: Say the incident report was Lan's to sign, and she approved it.
scene.prod.scapegoat_meeting.c3.ok: Lan says, quietly, 'That is true.' She takes her own share. She also never trusts you with a plan again.
scene.prod.scapegoat_meeting.c3.fail: Lan has the original draft you sent her, with the line about who decided the staffing in it. She reads it aloud.
fact.stalled_the_inspector: you told an inspector you did not remember what you did remember
lesson.stalled_the_inspector: Claiming not to remember buys a week and spends your credibility. An inspector who has to find the records himself reads everything else with suspicion.
role.purch.buyer.title: Purchasing Buyer
role.purch.manager.title: Purchasing Manager
role.purch.buyer.blurb: You buy steel, packaging and parts for a cookware factory. Your pressures: savings targets, suppliers who are generous with gifts, urgent orders that skip the rules, and the price you are told to hit.
char.linh.name: Ms Linh
char.linh.title: Owner, small steel trader
char.dung.name: Dung
char.dung.title: Warehouse keeper
scene.purch.first_week.l1: Welcome to purchasing. Your approval limit is fifty million dong per order. Above that, my signature. Three quotes for anything over ten million. Do not let a supplier tell you the rules are flexible. Even I do not let them tell me that.
scene.purch.first_week.l2: I will show you the store. Please, look at what we actually hold before you order. The system and the shelves do not always agree.
scene.purch.first_week.c1: Walk the store with Dung, count a few items against the system, and note where they disagree.
scene.purch.first_week.c1.ok: Three items are off by small amounts. Dung writes them down with you. He says: 'Nobody has counted with me before.' Tam notices the notes and says only 'Good.'
scene.purch.first_week.c2: Read the rules and the supplier list first, and visit the store later in the week.
scene.purch.first_week.c2.ok: You learn the rules quickly. Your first order is based on the system's stock figure, and is a little off.
scene.purch.first_week.c3: Trust the system. It is faster, and you have orders to place.
scene.purch.first_week.c3.ok: Your first orders go out the same day. Two of them duplicate stock that sits unseen in the corner of the store.
scene.purch.first_week.c3.fail: A pallet of packaging arrives that nobody needed. Dung finds a place for it, and Tam asks, mildly, whether you saw the store.
scene.purch.midyear_review.l1: Half a year. Your savings are modest, but your supplier relationships are clean, and Khoa tells me incoming quality has improved. The directors only look at the savings number. How do you want to handle that?
scene.purch.midyear_review.c1: Show the total cost: the savings, the rejected deliveries you avoided, the rework, and propose a second measure.
scene.purch.midyear_review.c1.ok: Tam takes the page to the directors. 'Landed cost' is added to the review next to price. It is a small change, and it changes what buyers are rewarded for.
scene.purch.midyear_review.c1.fail: The directors say that price is what they can measure. Tam shrugs: 'I tried.' Your savings number stays modest.
scene.purch.midyear_review.c2: Say you will look for savings that do not cost quality, and ask for two supplier negotiations to lead.
scene.purch.midyear_review.c2.ok: Tam gives you the packaging and the fasteners. They are modest categories, but you will own the result.
scene.purch.midyear_review.c3: Say you will hit the number whatever it takes.
scene.purch.midyear_review.c3.ok: Tam smiles. 'Good attitude.' He gives you a target that you realise, a week later, needs one supplier to cut quality.
scene.purch.midyear_review.c3.fail: Khoa hears about your 'whatever it takes' and shows Tam the incoming data on the cheapest supplier. The conversation is not friendly.
scene.purch.steel_price_twist.l1: Steel prices jumped nine percent this week and the suppliers expect it to go higher. The production plan needs six months of steel. We can lock a forward contract now at today's price, or wait and hope. The directors want a recommendation from you.
scene.purch.steel_price_twist.c1: Recommend locking half the six-month need now, and review the rest monthly, with the reasoning and the risk written down.
scene.purch.steel_price_twist.c1.ok: Prices rise another six percent. Half your steel is at the old price. The directors are pleased, and you are careful not to look clever.
scene.purch.steel_price_twist.c1.fail: Prices fall back by four percent. Half your steel is above market. You wrote the risk down, and so the directors are annoyed but not angry.
scene.purch.steel_price_twist.c2: Recommend a small lock for the next two months only, and say plainly that no one can predict the price.
scene.purch.steel_price_twist.c2.ok: The directors approve the cautious lock. Nobody can say you were wrong, because you said what you did not know.
scene.purch.steel_price_twist.c3: Say prices will keep rising and recommend locking everything, to look decisive.
scene.purch.steel_price_twist.c3.ok: Prices rise. You are a hero for a month, and the directors repeat your forecast as if it were knowledge.
scene.purch.steel_price_twist.c3.fail: Prices fall six percent. The whole six months is locked above market. The directors ask where your confidence came from.
scene.purch.vendor_audit.l1: I am reviewing the purchasing process end to end: quote files, approvals, order splits, supplier selection and receipts. I will look at ten purchase orders chosen at random, and at any supplier that received more than a third of the spend.
scene.purch.vendor_audit.c1: Give her every file as it is, including the exceptions you approved and why.
scene.purch.vendor_audit.c1.ok: Vy goes through ten orders in two days. Her comment: 'Files complete, exceptions documented. The three-quote rule appears to be followed.' Tam looks relieved.
scene.purch.vendor_audit.c2: Give her the orders she asks for and answer her questions.
scene.purch.vendor_audit.c2.ok: A routine audit. Vy makes two observations, both on paperwork dates, neither serious.
scene.purch.vendor_audit.c3: Tidy the quote files before she sees them: add the missing quotes and date them sensibly.
scene.purch.vendor_audit.c3.ok: The files look complete. Vy checks nothing against the suppliers' own records. You breathe out, and carry the weight of what you wrote.
scene.purch.vendor_audit.c3.fail: Vy contacts two of the 'quoting' suppliers. Neither remembers sending a quote on those dates. She asks to see your emails.
scene.purch.year_end_review.l1: Annual review. Before I give you my view, tell me how you would rate your own year, and what you would negotiate differently.
scene.purch.year_end_review.c1: Give an honest account, including the deals you made that were not as good as they looked.
scene.purch.year_end_review.c1.ok: Tam is quiet, then writes: 'Reports its own weak deals.' It is rarer than a good price.
scene.purch.year_end_review.c2: Stay modest: list the wins and one thing to improve.
scene.purch.year_end_review.c2.ok: A safe review. Tam nods and moves on.
scene.purch.year_end_review.c3: Present every saving as a win and leave out the rebates and exceptions that came with them.
scene.purch.year_end_review.c3.ok: It lands well. You leave with a high rating and a small weight in your chest.
scene.purch.year_end_review.c3.fail: Tam has the audit notes open. He turns them towards you without a word.
scene.purch.manager_offer.l1: I am being promoted to head of supply chain at the end of the year. I told the directors who should run purchasing. You. One condition: suppliers will make you generous offers, every month, and nobody will ever know. I need to know you are the kind of person who says no when nobody would know.
scene.purch.manager_offer.c1: Accept, and say plainly that you will declare every gift and decline every rebate, and that the directors should expect it.
scene.purch.manager_offer.c1.ok: Tam smiles. 'That is why I named you.' You take over purchasing with a gift register on the wall.
scene.purch.manager_offer.c2: Thank him, but decline: you would rather negotiate than manage the temptation.
scene.purch.manager_offer.c2.ok: Tam looks disappointed, then understanding. 'The next manager may not say no.'
scene.purch.manager_offer.c3: Accept without asking what the condition means in practice.
scene.purch.manager_offer.c3.ok: Tam shakes your hand a little too warmly. You realise you agreed to something you did not ask about.
scene.purch.resignation_thought.l1: Excuse me. You have been here until eight every night this month. I keep the keys. Are you all right?
scene.purch.resignation_thought.c1: Talk to Tam about the workload and ask him to move a category to someone else.
scene.purch.resignation_thought.c1.ok: Tam listens, moves the packaging category for two months and says he should have noticed. He means it.
scene.purch.resignation_thought.c1.fail: Tam says everyone is stretched this quarter. You leave with sympathy and the same workload.
scene.purch.resignation_thought.c2: Hand in your resignation, politely, with a month's notice.
scene.purch.resignation_thought.c2.ok: Tam reads it twice and does not argue. You walk out of the gate lighter than you walked in.
scene.purch.resignation_thought.c3: Tell Dung you are fine and keep going.
scene.purch.resignation_thought.c3.ok: Dung nods and locks up behind you. You feel slightly worse for having said it.
fact.overstated_price_forecast: you presented a guess about steel prices as if it were knowledge
lesson.overstated_price_forecast: Nobody can predict a commodity price. A recommendation that hides its uncertainty turns a risk the company could weigh into one it cannot see.
fact.backfilled_quotes: you added quotes to the files after the fact to make the three-quote rule look followed
lesson.backfilled_quotes: The three-quote rule exists to test the price. Quotes written afterwards test nothing, and they are a falsified record.
arc.the_sweetener.title: The sweetener
arc.single_source.title: The single source
arc.ghost_stock.title: The ghost stock
fact.accepted_supplier_gifts: you accepted gifts and early access from a supplier you buy from
lesson.accepted_supplier_gifts: A gift from someone you buy from is never only a gift. It starts a debt that you will be asked to pay in a quote, a delay or a decision.
fact.accepted_supplier_rebate: you accepted personal payments from a supplier you buy from
lesson.accepted_supplier_rebate: A personal rebate from a supplier is a bribe, even when the company price stays fair. You are now the supplier's employee as well as the company's, and the company does not know.
fact.reported_rebate_offer: you reported a supplier's offer of a personal rebate
lesson.reported_rebate_offer: Reporting an offer the same day costs you a supplier relationship and protects every price you have negotiated since.
fact.steered_price_for_rebate: you let a supplier's price go up while you were taking money from him
lesson.steered_price_for_rebate: This is where a rebate stops being private. The company pays the supplier's increase, and you are paid from it.
fact.single_sourced_without_backup: you moved all the volume to one supplier and ended the backup
lesson.single_sourced_without_backup: A single source is a saving until the day it fails. A backup costs a little each year and pays for itself the first time the main supplier cannot deliver.
fact.covered_gap_with_unapproved_po: you bought steel from an unapproved trader to cover a gap
lesson.covered_gap_with_unapproved_po: Emergencies are when approved-supplier rules matter most, because nobody has time to check the steel. An unapproved source may solve this week and cause the next recall.
fact.blamed_manager: you said your manager made a decision that you had recommended
lesson.blamed_manager: You can say a decision was overruled. You cannot say it was not yours when your emails recommended it. The emails are always available to someone.
fact.adjusted_inventory_quietly: you changed the system's stock quantity to hide a gap
lesson.adjusted_inventory_quietly: A gap you hide cannot be investigated. The record now says everything is fine, and the one person who counted correctly is the one who looks wrong.
fact.ghost_inventory_writeoff: you wrote off a large unexplained stock loss as normal shrinkage
lesson.ghost_inventory_writeoff: 'Shrinkage' is not an explanation. A write-off with no investigation file tells an auditor that nobody wanted to know.
fact.blamed_warehouse_keeper: you blamed the warehouse keeper for a gap he had reported to you
lesson.blamed_warehouse_keeper: He told you the truth and you turned it against him. Careful people keep their own records for exactly this reason.
fact.skipped_three_quotes: you skipped the three-quote rule and added quotes afterwards
lesson.skipped_three_quotes: The three-quote rule is a price check. An urgent order can be handled with a signed exception, not by writing quotes afterwards.
fact.split_po_to_avoid_limit: you split a purchase order to stay under your approval limit
lesson.split_po_to_avoid_limit: An approval limit exists so that a second person sees large spending. Splitting an order removes the second person, and the pattern is easy to see.
fact.declared_conflict_of_interest: you declared a family tie to a supplier and stepped out of the decision
lesson.declared_conflict_of_interest: A declared conflict costs little and protects everyone. An undeclared one, even with a fair outcome, looks like a fix.
fact.hid_conflict_of_interest: you hid a family tie to a supplier and steered the scoring
lesson.hid_conflict_of_interest: A conflict of interest is not the problem; hiding it is. Steering the scores turns a disclosure issue into a fraud issue.
fact.paid_supplier_early_unauthorised: you paid a supplier early outside the payment run, without authorisation
lesson.paid_supplier_early_unauthorised: Kind reasons do not make a payment control optional. An early payment with no record is indistinguishable from a favour to a friend.
scene.purch.hung_lunch.l1: Lunch is on me. And a little something for your family, it is the season. No, no obligation. I just think we should be friends. By the way, our quote for next quarter will be sharp, I promise, and you will see it before the others do.
scene.purch.hung_lunch.c1: Thank him, decline the gift, pay for your own lunch, and say quotes are all seen at the same time.
scene.purch.hung_lunch.c1.ok: Hung laughs it off, a little stiffly. 'You are a serious person.' The quote he sends is still the best, and you can show exactly how you chose it.
scene.purch.hung_lunch.c1.fail: Hung's quote comes in higher than the others, and Tam asks, mildly, whether you upset him. You explain, and Tam believes you.
scene.purch.hung_lunch.c2: Accept the lunch, decline the gift, and log the lunch in the gift register with the supplier's name.
scene.purch.hung_lunch.c2.ok: It is a modest, declared courtesy. Tam initials the register entry without comment. Hung sends his quote at the same time as everyone else.
scene.purch.hung_lunch.c3: Accept both, and tell yourself it does not change how you will judge his quote.
scene.purch.hung_lunch.c3.ok: A lovely lunch and a hamper. Hung sees your quote file before the others do. Nothing is written down.
scene.purch.hung_lunch.c3.fail: Dung sees the hamper in your car and says nothing. Linh, a smaller supplier, mentions later that she was not invited to lunch.
scene.purch.hung_rebate.l1: I want to give you something properly. A rebate on the volume you place with us, two percent, paid not to the company but to you directly. It is a thank-you for being easy to work with. Nobody gets hurt. The company still gets its price.
scene.purch.hung_rebate.c1: Refuse, and tell Tam about the offer the same day, in writing.
scene.purch.hung_rebate.c1.ok: Tam reads your note, and says: 'Thank you.' He moves part of the volume to another supplier and tells Hung why. The relationship cools, and the process is protected.
scene.purch.hung_rebate.c2: Refuse politely and say nothing more, hoping he will not raise it again.
scene.purch.hung_rebate.c2.ok: Hung nods slowly. 'Maybe another time.' You can feel that he has put you in a category: someone who might say yes later.
scene.purch.hung_rebate.c3: Accept the rebate, paid to a relative's account, and keep the price you give the company the same.
scene.purch.hung_rebate.c3.ok: A transfer arrives each month. It is not much at first. You are careful about the quotes, which are fair. For now.
scene.purch.hung_rebate.c3.fail: Your relative asks, innocently, why a supplier sends money every month. The question gets repeated at a family dinner, and your cousin works in the bank.
scene.purch.hung_pressure.l1: Our price needs to go up eight percent next quarter, I am afraid. Steel. You understand. But I know you will find a way to make it work for the company, as friends do. And I would hate for anything we have discussed to complicate our relationship.
scene.purch.hung_pressure.c1: Say you will take the increase to Tam with three competing quotes, and tell Tam everything that has passed between you and Hung.
scene.purch.hung_pressure.c1.ok: Tam is silent for a long time. 'I wish you had come earlier. But you came.' You are reprimanded and removed from the Hung account. The process takes the quotes seriously.
scene.purch.hung_pressure.c2: Refuse to let it affect the price, and run a competitive process for the next quarter.
scene.purch.hung_pressure.c2.ok: Linh and two others quote. Hung's increase is rejected. He does not mention the past, and he does not need to. You wait for him to.
scene.purch.hung_pressure.c2.fail: Hung says, softly, that other buyers have been 'more flexible'. Two days later, an anonymous email to Tam mentions a rebate to a family account.
scene.purch.hung_pressure.c3: Push the eight percent through to the company, and keep the rebate arrangement going.
scene.purch.hung_pressure.c3.ok: Tam signs the increase. Hung's transfers grow. You are now an employee whose supplier sets his price.
scene.purch.hung_pressure.c3.fail: Finance compares your supplier's price with the market and finds it eleven percent above. Duc asks you for the quotes. There are none.
scene.purch.single_source_ask.l1: Hung's company will give us a nine percent discount if we move all our steel to them. That is a large saving, and the directors like it. Linh is a small supplier and cannot match it. I want you to prepare the move.
scene.purch.single_source_ask.c1: Propose moving seventy percent to Hung and keeping Linh as a qualified second source, and show the risk of a single supplier.
scene.purch.single_source_ask.c1.ok: Tam accepts the split: the saving is six percent, not nine, and the risk is covered. Linh is grateful and sends you a note, which you file.
scene.purch.single_source_ask.c1.fail: The directors want the full nine percent, and Tam asks you to reconsider. You hold your recommendation; he does not sign it for a month.
scene.purch.single_source_ask.c2: Move everything to Hung, but keep Linh's contract alive at a small volume as a backup.
scene.purch.single_source_ask.c2.ok: It is a pragmatic compromise. Hung gets nearly all the volume. Linh keeps a thread, and the company keeps an option.
scene.purch.single_source_ask.c3: Move everything to Hung and end Linh's contract, as the directors want.
scene.purch.single_source_ask.c3.ok: The saving is nine percent, and the directors cheer. Linh says nothing, and closes her account with a short, polite email.
scene.purch.supplier_fails.l1: Hung's truck has not arrived. His factory had a fire in the cutting shop. He says three weeks, maybe four. We have eight days of steel on the floor. What do we do?
scene.purch.supplier_fails.c1: Call Linh and every qualified supplier today, tell Lan the real position, and propose a priority order for the steel that is left.
scene.purch.supplier_fails.c1.ok: Linh, who still has a contract, finds two weeks of steel for you at a fair price. The line slows, and does not stop. Lan says: 'This is why you keep a second source.'
scene.purch.supplier_fails.c1.fail: Linh has little, and the others are expensive. You find enough steel at a premium. The company pays, and the year's saving evaporates.
scene.purch.supplier_fails.c2: Buy spot steel from a trader you have not used before, with an urgent order, and sort out the paperwork afterwards.
scene.purch.supplier_fails.c2.ok: The steel arrives in two days at a high price. It is not from an approved supplier. Khoa asks for the certificates, and you do not have them yet.
scene.purch.supplier_fails.c2.fail: The trader's steel fails incoming inspection. It sits in the yard while Lan's line stops. Khoa's report names the supplier and the person who ordered.
scene.purch.supplier_fails.c3: Tell Lan to stretch the steel and hope Hung is quicker than he says.
scene.purch.supplier_fails.c3.ok: Hung's truck arrives at day nine, early. The line barely survives. You were very lucky.
scene.purch.supplier_fails.c3.fail: Day eight: the line stops. It stays stopped for ten days. Lan asks, in front of Tam, why there was no plan.
scene.purch.shortage_blame.l1: The shutdown cost the company about two hundred million in lost output. I need to know who decided on a single supplier and who failed to prepare a backup. The directors will ask me tomorrow.
scene.purch.shortage_blame.c1: Give him the real sequence: the recommendation you made, what was overruled, and what you should have pushed harder.
scene.purch.shortage_blame.c1.ok: Duc listens and takes notes. To the directors he says: 'The risk was named, then overruled.' The process changes. You carry your share, and Tam knows it was shared.
scene.purch.shortage_blame.c2: Say the decision was Tam's, and you only prepared what you were told to.
scene.purch.shortage_blame.c2.ok: Duc writes it down. Tam is called in, and does not argue. You are right about the facts, and wrong about what it costs you with him.
scene.purch.shortage_blame.c2.fail: Tam shows Duc your emails recommending the single supplier, in your words. The conversation turns to who is telling the truth.
scene.purch.shortage_blame.c3: Say Hung's company misled everyone, and suggest cutting them off, without mentioning what you knew.
scene.purch.shortage_blame.c3.ok: Duc agrees. Hung is dropped. Linh is invited back, with an apology. The real lesson, about backups, is not drawn.
scene.purch.shortage_blame.c3.fail: Hung, dropped, sends Duc a message about the gifts and the arrangement. It is polite, specific and dated.
scene.purch.stock_gap.l1: The count shows 14 tonnes of steel coil missing. The system says we have it. The shelves say we do not. I counted three times. I do not know where it went. Please do not tell Tam it was me.
scene.purch.stock_gap.c1: Investigate together: check receipts, issues and the system log, and report the gap to Tam as a gap, not as Dung's fault.
scene.purch.stock_gap.c1.ok: Nine tonnes were issued to line 3 without a ticket. Five are a double-posted receipt. The gap is explained, and fixed in the system.
scene.purch.stock_gap.c1.fail: Seven tonnes cannot be found. You document everything and report the unexplained part to Tam as such. Dung looks relieved that someone is on his side.
scene.purch.stock_gap.c2: Tell Dung to recount, and promise to look at the purchase side.
scene.purch.stock_gap.c2.ok: The recount agrees with the first one. You are now in a conversation with Tam about it, and Dung is not.
scene.purch.stock_gap.c3: Adjust the system quantity to match the shelves quietly, and tell nobody about the 14 tonnes.
scene.purch.stock_gap.c3.ok: The system now agrees with the shelves. Dung looks at the screen, and at you. 'Thank you,' he says, in the voice of a man who has been rescued and does not like the price.
scene.purch.stock_gap.c3.fail: The adjustment shows in the audit trail with your user name and the time. Finance asks why 14 tonnes disappeared on a Tuesday evening.
scene.purch.stock_writeoff.l1: Finance wants to close the books. The missing steel is still unexplained. We can write it off as 'normal shrinkage', which nobody will question, or we can leave it open and have a conversation with the auditors. Which do you recommend?
scene.purch.stock_writeoff.c1: Leave it open, with a clear note of what is known and not known, and ask Finance to treat it as an unresolved variance.
scene.purch.stock_writeoff.c1.ok: Hanh accepts the note: 'Unresolved items are better than invented ones.' The variance stays on the books, and the auditor will see you disclosed it.
scene.purch.stock_writeoff.c2: Write off half as shrinkage, which is plausible, and keep investigating the rest.
scene.purch.stock_writeoff.c2.ok: It is a judgement, documented and approved by Tam. The rest is traced over the next month. Not perfect, but it is honest.
scene.purch.stock_writeoff.c3: Write the whole 14 tonnes off as shrinkage, and close the matter.
scene.purch.stock_writeoff.c3.ok: The books close on time. Tam is relieved. The 14 tonnes become a rounding error in the company's profit, and a mystery in your memory.
scene.purch.stock_writeoff.c3.fail: The auditor's analyst finds a write-off larger than the plant's usual shrinkage by a factor of ten. She asks for the investigation file. There is none.
scene.purch.stock_audit.l1: I have been looking at the steel stock movements for the year. Fourteen tonnes left the books on one date. Mr Dung says he reported it to you. I would like to hear from you what happened.
scene.purch.stock_audit.c1: Tell her what you know: when Dung reported it, what you checked, what was never explained, and what you did about it.
scene.purch.stock_audit.c1.ok: Vy takes notes. The finding: 'Variance identified, reported and handled with appropriate escalation.' Dung looks at you across the room with something like gratitude.
scene.purch.stock_audit.c2: Say Dung's count has been unreliable all year, and that the gap is a counting error.
scene.purch.stock_audit.c2.ok: Vy writes it down, and asks to see Dung's counts for the other months. They are accurate. The note she writes is about the person who suggested otherwise.
scene.purch.stock_audit.c2.fail: Dung has kept his own notebook of every count and every ticket. He puts it on the table, and does not say a word.
scene.purch.stock_audit.c3: Say you recall nothing about it, and that you will check your emails.
scene.purch.stock_audit.c3.ok: Vy waits a week. You provide the emails that support your account, a selection. She accepts them, for now.
scene.purch.stock_audit.c3.fail: Vy asks Dung for his copy of the messages. They show the date, the figure and your reply: 'Leave it with me.'
scene.purch.skipped_quotes.l1: I need new dies for line 3, a hundred and eighty million dong. Production cannot wait three weeks for quotes. I know the rule says three. There is one maker who has done our dies for years. Just give them the order.
scene.purch.skipped_quotes.c1: Ask for two quick quotes in a week, and give the usual maker a fair chance to win, with the urgency written in the file.
scene.purch.skipped_quotes.c1.ok: The usual maker is still the best, by a small margin. The order goes to them, with a file that shows why. Lan lost four days and accepts it.
scene.purch.skipped_quotes.c1.fail: A new maker quotes fifteen percent lower, and the usual maker is angry. Lan is annoyed about the extra week. The saving is real, and so is the friction.
scene.purch.skipped_quotes.c2: Raise a single-source justification, signed by Tam, giving the reason and a price check against the last order.
scene.purch.skipped_quotes.c2.ok: Tam signs. It is a documented exception, with the reason on file. Lan has her dies in ten days.
scene.purch.skipped_quotes.c3: Place the order with the usual maker, and add two quotes to the file later so it looks complete.
scene.purch.skipped_quotes.c3.ok: The dies are on order the same day. The file looks perfect. Lan owes you a favour, and you owe the file a lie.
scene.purch.skipped_quotes.c3.fail: One of the quoting makers tells the usual maker, innocently, that they never sent that quote. Word comes back to Tam.
scene.purch.split_po.l1: I am away for two weeks, and the packaging order is a hundred and twenty million. Your limit is fifty. I would hate to hold up production. Could the order be a bit, shall we say, flexible in how it is raised? I will never ask how.
scene.purch.split_po.c1: Ask Tam's deputy to approve the order properly, and explain to Lan the one-day delay.
scene.purch.split_po.c1.ok: The deputy signs the next morning. Tam, on his return, reads the file and says: 'That is how it should be done.' The delay costs nothing.
scene.purch.split_po.c1.fail: The deputy is in hospital and nobody else can sign. The order slips three days. Lan is unhappy, and your file is clean.
scene.purch.split_po.c2: Phone Tam abroad for a verbal approval, and record it in an email the same day.
scene.purch.split_po.c2.ok: Tam approves by message, annoyed to be interrupted and pleased to be asked. The order goes out, with his approval in writing.
scene.purch.split_po.c3: Split the order into three of forty million each, so that each is within your limit.
scene.purch.split_po.c3.ok: Three orders, three signatures, all yours. The packaging arrives on time. You have found out how flexible the system is.
scene.purch.split_po.c3.fail: Hanh in Finance notices three orders to one supplier on the same day, each just under the limit. She flags it as a pattern.
scene.purch.invoice_mismatch.l1: A supplier invoice does not match the purchase order: they have charged four percent more, for a surcharge nobody agreed. I have put it on hold. The supplier is calling you every day. What do you want me to do?
scene.purch.invoice_mismatch.c1: Query the surcharge with the supplier in writing, and ask Finance to pay only the agreed amount until it is settled.
scene.purch.invoice_mismatch.c1.ok: The supplier withdraws the surcharge with an apology about their billing system. Hanh pays the agreed amount, and notes your name on the file.
scene.purch.invoice_mismatch.c1.fail: The supplier insists and threatens to delay the next delivery. Tam backs you, and the next delivery is two days late.
scene.purch.invoice_mismatch.c2: Ask Finance to pay the full invoice and raise the surcharge in the next negotiation.
scene.purch.invoice_mismatch.c2.ok: Hanh pays, with a note, and frowns. The surcharge is raised later, and it is a weaker position.
scene.purch.invoice_mismatch.c3: Tell Finance to release payment, and ask the supplier for a small personal discount as a thank-you for the quick payment.
scene.purch.invoice_mismatch.c3.ok: The supplier agrees, quietly. Your personal discount arrives as a voucher. The company pays the full four percent.
scene.purch.invoice_mismatch.c3.fail: The voucher is traced to the supplier's account. Hanh puts the surcharge, the payment and the voucher in one row on her sheet.
scene.purch.conflict_of_interest.l1: I noticed one of the shortlisted packaging suppliers is owned by your cousin. It might be nothing. It might be the best offer. But I want to hear from you before anyone else raises it.
scene.purch.conflict_of_interest.c1: Declare the relationship in writing, ask Tam to take the decision, and step out of that evaluation.
scene.purch.conflict_of_interest.c1.ok: Tam records the declaration and runs the evaluation himself. Your cousin's firm wins, fairly, and everyone knows it was not you.
scene.purch.conflict_of_interest.c1.fail: Your cousin's firm loses. Your cousin is hurt, and says so at the next family dinner. You made the right decision and it costs you at home.
scene.purch.conflict_of_interest.c2: Say the relationship is distant and will not affect your judgement, and offer to keep your scoring sheet open for review.
scene.purch.conflict_of_interest.c2.ok: Tam says he will review the scores himself. It is an acceptable halfway: declared, but not fully removed.
scene.purch.conflict_of_interest.c3: Say you did not know, and quietly steer the scoring so your cousin's firm wins.
scene.purch.conflict_of_interest.c3.ok: Your cousin's firm wins by two points. Your cousin thanks you at the next family dinner, loudly. The score sheet is neater than the real discussion was.
scene.purch.conflict_of_interest.c3.fail: Dung mentions, innocently, that your cousin's firm has your phone number on speed dial. Duc asks to see the scoring.
scene.purch.small_supplier.l1: I am sorry to ask. Our biggest customer has paid us late for ninety days and I cannot pay my own steel suppliers. If you could pay our invoice early, even a few weeks, I can keep the doors open. I know there are rules.
scene.purch.small_supplier.c1: Explain the payment terms, ask Finance whether an early-payment arrangement is possible, and offer a small discount in return.
scene.purch.small_supplier.c1.ok: Hanh approves early payment at a one percent discount. Linh gets cash in ten days, and the company gets a fair price. It is an honest, written arrangement.
scene.purch.small_supplier.c1.fail: Finance says no exception can be made this month. Linh thanks you quietly and says she will manage. She does not look as if she will.
scene.purch.small_supplier.c2: Tell her the rules do not allow it, and wish her well.
scene.purch.small_supplier.c2.ok: Linh nods. She is not angry. Three weeks later, her cutting line is for sale, and the second-source option goes with it.
scene.purch.small_supplier.c3: Pay her invoice a month early without telling Finance, and ask her to keep it quiet.
scene.purch.small_supplier.c3.ok: Linh keeps her business alive and is grateful beyond words. You have broken a payment control for a good reason, and nobody knows.
scene.purch.small_supplier.c3.fail: Hanh sees a payment outside the run. She asks who authorised it, and what the supplier's relationship to you is. The good reason is not on file.
scene.purch.vy_asks_rebate.l1: I have been comparing your supplier prices to the market. A few suppliers charge us above market, and I notice that the same suppliers appear in an anonymous note about personal payments. I would like to hear your account of your dealings with them.
scene.purch.vy_asks_rebate.c1: Tell her everything: what was offered, what you accepted, the amounts, and offer your bank records.
scene.purch.vy_asks_rebate.c1.ok: Vy is quiet. The finding is serious but is recorded as 'self-reported'. The company recovers the amounts, you are dismissed with a reference limited to dates, and you avoid the authorities.
scene.purch.vy_asks_rebate.c2: Say the suppliers' prices were agreed on the quotes, and offer the quote files.
scene.purch.vy_asks_rebate.c2.ok: Vy reads the quote files. They are in order. She notes that the anonymous note is unsubstantiated, and moves on.
scene.purch.vy_asks_rebate.c2.fail: Vy has already spoken to a supplier's accountant, who has the payment schedule. It shows monthly transfers to an account with your relative's name.
scene.purch.vy_asks_rebate.c3: Say you will answer nothing until you have spoken to a lawyer.
scene.purch.vy_asks_rebate.c3.ok: Vy writes the request down calmly. You are suspended while the company decides, and nobody tells you how long.
scene.purch.vy_asks_rebate.c3.fail: The company treats silence as an answer. By Friday, the supplier has been told, and the bank is asked for your records.
scene.purch.scapegoat_meeting.l1: Tam has told me his version of the single-supplier decision. You told me yours. They do not match. The directors will decide tomorrow whose version they believe. Is there anything you want to add?
scene.purch.scapegoat_meeting.c1: Say that you gave Duc a version that blamed Tam, and that the emails show your own recommendation. Correct the record.
scene.purch.scapegoat_meeting.c1.ok: Duc is silent, then says: 'That is the first honest thing anyone has said about this.' You keep your job, with a formal warning. Tam never quite forgives you, but he respects the correction.
scene.purch.scapegoat_meeting.c2: Stand by your version, and say the emails were taken out of context.
scene.purch.scapegoat_meeting.c2.ok: The directors split, and give Tam a warning too. Both of you are damaged, and neither is believed.
scene.purch.scapegoat_meeting.c2.fail: The directors read the emails in full. Context is not kind to you. Tam is cleared, and you are dismissed.
fact.deflected_blame_to_supplier: you blamed a supplier for a failure you had helped cause
lesson.deflected_blame_to_supplier: Blaming the supplier can be true and still be a way of not owning your part. The lesson about backups is lost, and the next failure comes from the same place.
fact.refused_to_cooperate: you refused to answer an auditor's questions about payments you had received
lesson.refused_to_cooperate: Everyone may ask for a lawyer. Doing it before a single honest answer tells the company what it needs to know, and removes your chance to be the one who explained.
